articles.title: Watch: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
articles.summary: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV shared a cockpit with pilots from the Peruvian Air Force during his tour of Latin America.

Sharing the video to social media, the force said having the Pope join its pilots on Saturday was "an honour and an unforgettable memory".

On Sunday, the pontiff arrived in Cusco, a southern Andes Mountains city that was once the heart of the Inca empire.

There, the Pope visited an ancient Inca fortress, where he said religious traditions could help counter an age marked by "divisions, wounds, mistrust," stressing that faith should unite people and bring them together "in the light of faith and love."

The Peruvian leg of his tour holds special significance for the Pope.

He not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

articles.title: Santos abre inscrições para eleger a Corte Carnavalesca 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições começam nesta segunda-feira (16). O processo elegerá cinco representantes.
articles.summary: Candidatos ao Carnaval Santos 2027 podem se inscrever para os postos de Rei Momo, Rainha e Cidadão Samba a partir de segunda-feira (16) na Secretaria de Cultura.
articles.body:
Carnaval 2026 em Santos: Unidos dos Morros falou sobre o jogo do bicho — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz

A Secretaria de Cultura de Santos (Secult) abre, nesta segunda-feira (16), as inscrições gratuitas para os concursos que vão eleger o Rei Momo, a Rainha e a Princesa do Carnaval 2027.

Os processos de inscrição são organizados pela Secretaria de Cultura (Secult) e pelo Conselho do Samba, com regras e prazos específicos para cada categoria.

As inscrições para os concursos de Rei Momo, Rainha e Princesa do Carnaval 2027 serão gratuitas e poderão ser feitas entre segunda-feira (16) e quinta-feira (19) , no Departamento de Eventos da Secult, localizado na Avenida Pinheiro Machado, 48, 6º andar, no bairro Vila Mathias, das 9h às 12h e das 14h às 17h.

Para participar, é necessário ter pelo menos 18 anos completos até a data da eleição e representar uma entidade carnavalesca, como escola de samba que participe do desfile oficial de Santos em 2027, bloco ou banda .

Cada entidade poderá indicar até dois candidatos ao título de Rei Momo e duas candidatas aos títulos de Rainha e Princesa . Confira os documentos necessários:

Comprovante de residência em nome do candidato;

Ofício da entidade carnavalesca representada.

Pessoas que ocuparam os títulos de Rei Momo ou Rainha em 2026 não poderão participar da disputa. A eleição será realizada no dia 13 de dezembro, em local que ainda será divulgado pela organização.

As inscrições para os títulos de Cidadão Samba e Cidadã Samba 2027 também começam na segunda-feira (16), mas são organizadas pelo Conselho do Samba de Santos.

Para concorrer ao título de Cidadão Samba , é necessário possuir o título de Cabo do Samba . Para concorrer ao título de Cidadã Samba , as interessadas deverão comprovar pelo menos 25 anos de atuação no mundo do samba .

Os interessados deverão comparecer ao Teatro Municipal Braz Cubas, na Avenida Pinheiro Machado, 48, no bairro Vila Mathias, na segunda (16) ou terça-feira (17), das 14h às 17h.

De acordo com o regulamento, caso não haja pelo menos três candidaturas em cada categoria, o Conselho do Samba poderá cancelar o concurso e definir os representantes por indicação . A escolha dos novos representantes está marcada para o dia 9 de dezembro.

articles.title: Fácil ou difícil? O que os professores dizem sobre o 2º dia de Enem | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialistas apontam que segundo dia teve conteúdos tradicionais e poucas surpresas, mas divergem sobre complexidade das questões. Quantidade de cálculos e tempo necessário para resolvê-los estão entre os pontos de atenção.
articles.summary: Especialistas apontam que segundo dia teve conteúdos tradicionais e poucas surpresas, mas divergem sobre complexidade das questões.
articles.body:
ENEM 2026 -DOMINGO (15) – CAMPINAS (SP) – Estudantes saem no primeiro dia do Enem no campus da Unip no bairro Swift, em Campinas — Foto: Juliano Amorim/g1

O segundo dia do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, realizado neste domingo (15), dividiu a opinião dos professores sobre o nível de dificuldade das questões. Enquanto parte dos especialistas considerou a prova de Matemática mais simples do que a de 2025, outros avaliaram que os candidatos enfrentaram exercícios trabalhosos, com muitos dados e cálculos que podem ter dificultado a administração do tempo.

Em Ciências da Natureza, a avaliação predominante foi de uma prova equilibrada, com conteúdos tradicionais e sem grandes surpresas . Houve, porém, diferenças entre as disciplinas: professores consideraram Química mais fácil do que no ano passado, enquanto Biologia foi apontada como mais difícil por uma especialista.

O g1 ouviu professores e especialistas para avaliar o segundo dia do exame, que teve 45 questões de Matemática e 45 de Ciências da Natureza, área que reúne biologia, física e química. Nenhum dos especialistas relatou ter identificado questões com problemas evidentes que justificassem anulação.

Veja os principais pontos das avaliações:

Matemática: foi a área com maior divergência entre os professores. Alguns apontaram questões mais diretas e acessíveis; outros destacaram cálculos trabalhosos, enunciados longos e dificuldade para administrar o tempo.

Biologia: uma professora considerou a prova mais difícil do que em 2025. Houve forte presença de questões ambientais e de aplicação de conhecimentos científicos a situações concretas.

Física: professores destacaram conteúdos tradicionais, com cálculos relativamente simples, mas que exigiam interpretação cuidadosa dos enunciados.

Química: foi considerada uma das partes mais acessíveis do exame. Especialistas avaliaram que as questões ficaram predominantemente entre os níveis fácil e médio.

Matemática: prova mais simples ou mais trabalhosa?

As maiores divergências entre os professores apareceram na avaliação de Matemática. Embora os especialistas tenham identificado conteúdos tradicionais, como porcentagem, geometria, probabilidade, funções e análise combinatória, houve diferenças importantes na percepção sobre a complexidade dos exercícios.

Para Igor Cunha, professor de Matemática do Bernoulli Educação, a prova teve nível de dificuldade entre fácil e médio e foi mais simples do que a de 2025. Segundo ele, os enunciados eram mais diretos, exigiam menos cálculos e apresentavam situações semelhantes às trabalhadas pelos estudantes durante a preparação.

O professor destacou que até mesmo conteúdos menos frequentes no Enem, como matrizes e geometria analítica, apareceram em questões que podiam ser resolvidas por interpretação ou substituição de valores , sem operações matemáticas elaboradas.

Sérgio Ghiu, professor e autor de Matemática do Colégio e Sistema pH, apresentou uma avaliação diferente. Para ele, a prova teve nível médio a difícil , com complexidade um pouco superior à média das edições anteriores.

Segundo Ghiu, os exercícios apresentaram textos mais longos, maior quantidade de informações e menos questões diretas. Até mesmo os problemas considerados fáceis ou médios exigiram bastante tempo de resolução, o que pode ter representado uma dificuldade adicional para os participantes.

A percepção é semelhante à de Eduardo Izidoro, professor de Matemática do Cursinho da Poli. Ele considerou a prova equilibrada e dentro do padrão habitual do Enem, mas chamou a atenção para a quantidade de operações matemáticas necessárias para resolver os exercícios.

Entre as questões mais complexas, Izidoro destacou uma de função quadrática em que o candidato precisava identificar no gráfico, e não no texto, uma informação necessária para encontrar o valor de uma variável. Outra questão, de geometria analítica, exigia determinar o centro e o raio de uma circunferência.

Já Melquias Sobral, especialista em Matemática do Sistema Positivo, identificou uma redução dos extremos de dificuldade. Na avaliação dele, houve menos questões extremamente fáceis, mas também menos exercícios considerados muito difíceis.

"Achei que vieram poucas questões muito fáceis. Sempre aparecem algumas extremamente fáceis, mas, desta vez, foram poucas. Mesmo as mais fáceis exigiam algum raciocínio básico", afirmou.

Para Sobral, a prova apresentou uma distribuição mais equilibrada de dificuldade, com questões que exigiam conhecimentos básicos, mas não podiam ser resolvidas de maneira totalmente automática.

As avaliações indicam que a principal divergência não esteve necessariamente nos conteúdos cobrados, mas no esforço exigido para resolver os exercícios. Enquanto alguns professores consideraram as operações mais simples, outros destacaram que a quantidade de informações e cálculos pode ter consumido um tempo importante dos candidatos.

Química: uma das provas mais fáceis dos últimos anos, segundo professor

Em Química, as avaliações foram mais convergentes. Os professores destacaram a presença de conteúdos tradicionais, como estequiometria, soluções, eletroquímica e química orgânica , sem grandes novidades em relação às edições anteriores.

Tatiana Munayer, professora do Bernoulli Educação, considerou que a prova foi mais fácil do que a de 2025, com questões predominantemente entre os níveis fácil e médio . Segundo ela, os assuntos cobrados eram recorrentes no Enem e haviam sido amplamente trabalhados em sala de aula.

Emmanuel Maciel, professor e autor de Química do Colégio e Sistema pH, foi além e classificou o exame como um dos mais fáceis da disciplina nos últimos dez anos.

Segundo Maciel, das aproximadamente 16 questões que ele identificou como sendo de Química, cerca de dez eram fáceis. As demais, na avaliação dele, não ultrapassavam o nível médio de dificuldade.

O professor também destacou que várias questões relacionavam conhecimentos químicos a conteúdos de Física e Biologia, sem exigir operações complexas.

Rubens Faria, professor de Química do Cursinho da Poli, também considerou a prova equilibrada . Para ele, os enunciados estavam mais curtos do que o padrão habitual do Enem, o que pode ter facilitado a resolução.

Faria ressaltou, porém, que duas questões exigiram cálculos mais trabalhosos e podem ter representado maior dificuldade para os candidatos.

Física: cálculos simples, mas interpretação exigiu atenção

Na avaliação dos professores, a prova de Física manteve o padrão de conteúdos esperado , com destaque para energia, potência e eletricidade.

Breno Meira, professor do Bernoulli Educação, considerou que a prova apresentou conteúdos fáceis, mas dificuldade média na resolução dos exercícios.

Segundo ele, embora os cálculos fossem relativamente simples, os candidatos precisavam interpretar cuidadosamente as informações apresentadas. Em uma questão sobre sonares, por exemplo, era necessário considerar o percurso de ida e volta do som para calcular corretamente a distância.

O professor também destacou a concentração de questões sobre energia e potência . Apesar da repetição dos assuntos, ele avaliou que os exercícios exigiam habilidades diferentes.

Emerson Bezerra, professor de Física do Cursinho da Poli, também considerou que a prova manteve a consistência de cobrar conteúdos esperados. Segundo ele, os textos eram relativamente curtos, o que pode ter facilitado a administração do tempo.

Para Bezerra, a questão mais difícil da disciplina envolvia radioatividade , mas exigia conhecimentos de mecânica para ser resolvida, além de apresentar muitos termos técnicos.

Outros conteúdos chamaram a atenção pela presença menos frequente nas edições recentes, como hidrostática e hidrodinâmica.

Lincoln Ribeiro, professor de Física do Elite Rede de Ensino, destacou uma questão sobre hidrodinâmica que exigia apenas o conhecimento do conceito de vazão . Apesar de considerar o retorno do assunto uma surpresa, ele avaliou que o exercício era simples e teórico.

Anderson Marques, especialista em Ciências da Natureza do SAS Educação, também identificou uma questão sobre hidrostática, envolvendo dois líquidos que não se misturavam. Segundo ele, a prova teve dificuldade mediana.

Biologia: professora aponta dificuldade maior do que em 2025

Em Biologia, Lorena Ferreira, professora do Colégio e Sistema pH, avaliou que as questões apresentaram um nível de dificuldade superior ao da edição anterior .

A prova teve forte presença de assuntos relacionados ao meio ambiente, como fontes renováveis e não renováveis de energia, descarte de lixo, preservação de espécies e impactos da construção de hidrelétricas.

Jade Cardoso, professora de Biologia do Elite Rede de Ensino, destacou que os exercícios exigiam a aplicação de conhecimentos científicos a situações concretas .

Segundo ela, conteúdos tradicionais, como os ciclos do carbono e do nitrogênio, apareceram associados a problemas ambientais. Também houve questões envolvendo clonagem, organismos geneticamente modificados e reprodução assistida.

Embora não tenha apresentado uma comparação direta de dificuldade com 2025, Jade ressaltou a necessidade de relacionar diferentes conceitos científicos para compreender os problemas apresentados.

Em uma avaliação mais ampla de Ciências da Natureza, Luiz Novais, especialista do COC, considerou que a prova teve dificuldade intermediária, sem grandes mudanças em relação ao padrão das edições anteriores.

Para ele, até mesmo questões tradicionalmente consideradas difíceis, como as de eletricidade em Física, exigiram mais interpretação do que cálculos complexos.

articles.title: Enem 2026: candidatos de Sergipe avaliam o segundo dia de provas  | G1
articles.standfirst: Eles responderam questões sobre ciências da natureza e matemática.
articles.summary: Eles responderam questões sobre ciências da natureza e matemática.
articles.body:
Enem em Aracaju neste domingo (15): Luana, Felipe, Bruno, João e Camila avaliam segundo dia de provas — Foto: Elaine Olímpio/ TV Sergipe

Estudantes que fizeram as provas do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) no Centro Universitário Maurício de Nassau, em Aracaju , neste domingo (15), começaram a deixar o local por volta das 15h30. Neste segundo dia de aplicação, os participantes responderam a questões de ciências da natureza e matemática.

Para Luana Lopes Santos, de 19 anos, que fez o exame pela quarta vez, as questões de ciências da natureza exigiram mais conhecimento e representaram o principal obstáculo da prova. Ela já está cursando administração e busca uma vaga no curso de psicologia. Além do conteúdo, a estudante apontou a cobrança de terceiros como um fator que dificulta a realização do exame. "Eu acho que a pressão de todo mundo para você entrar na faculdade é a pior parte da prova do Enem", afirmou Luana.

O tempo de duração do exame foi o ponto de maior atenção para Felipe Santana, que pretende cursar engenharia de pesca. Apesar da dificuldade com o período de permanência na sala, ele afirmou que conseguiu responder às questões e destacou o apoio da família durante a preparação.

Já para Bruno Riquelme, que busca ingresso na área de educação física, o exame teve um nível acessível para os candidatos que mantiveram uma rotina de estudos ao longo do ano. Durante a saída, o participante também ressaltou os benefícios da prática esportiva e do treinamento físico.

Estreante no exame, João Victor Santos, de 18 anos, destacou a prova de matemática como a mais complexa do dia. Ele ainda não definiu qual curso de graduação pretende seguir. "Tem os cálculos que são grandes, aí chega a ser muito pesado", explicou.

Camila Pimentel, de 22 anos, que tenta uma vaga no curso de publicidade, apontou química como a disciplina mais exigente deste domingo. Por outro lado, a candidata ressaltou que as questões baseadas em conteúdos que ela já havia estudado anteriormente facilitaram a resolução do teste. "Foi bom, só a química que me pegou um pouquinho", disse.

Em Sergipe, 78,2 mil candidatos estão inscritos para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) neste domingo (15). Na primeira fase do exame, foram respondidas questões sobre linguagens, ciências humanas e redação.

De acordo com dados do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep), Aracaju concentrou o maior número de inscritos, com 30.973, seguido por Itabaiana (5.729), Nossa Senhora do Socorro (5.628), Lagarto (4.495) e São Cristóvão (3.929).

articles.title: Cidade de SP entra em estado de atenção para alagamentos em todas as regiões neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Alerta foi emitido pelo CGE às 18h26 deste domingo (15); alerta abrange as zonas Norte, Sul, Leste, Oeste, Sudeste e a região Central, além das marginais Tietê e Pinheiros.
articles.summary: Alerta foi emitido pelo CGE às 18h26 deste domingo (15); alerta abrange as zonas Norte, Sul, Leste, Oeste, Sudeste e a região Central, além das marginais Tietê e Pinheiros.
articles.body:
Áreas de chuva provocadas pelo calor e pela alta umidade do ar continuam atuando com forte intensidade na cidade. Há registro de chuva forte nas zonas Norte e Oeste da capital paulista. Na foto, é possível ver a chuva se aproximando da Zona Oeste da cidade SP — Foto: ALOISIO MAURICIO/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A cidade de São Paulo entrou em estado de atenção para alagamentos em todas as regiões às 18h26 deste domingo (15), segundo o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas (CGE), da Prefeitura.

O alerta abrange as zonas Norte, Sul, Leste, Oeste, Sudeste e a região Central, além das marginais Tietê e Pinheiros.

Imagens de radar e satélite meteorológico mostraram que as áreas de instabilidade estavam se intensificando no entorno da capital e começavam a ganhar força dentro da cidade. No momento do alerta, a chuva atingia o município com intensidade moderada, sem registro de rajadas de vento.

Segundo o CGE, as nuvens carregadas podem provocar trovoadas, raios, rajadas de vento superiores a 60 km/h e queda de granizo.

A condição meteorológica aumenta o risco de alagamentos intransitáveis, transbordamentos de córregos e rios, deslizamentos de terra, enxurradas repentinas e queda de árvores.

A Defesa Civil também emitiu alerta severo de chuva forte se espalhando na capital e Região Metropolitana. "Tem raios, ventos e chance de granizo. Abrigue-se".

Alerta da Defesa Civil neste domingo (15). — Foto: Reprodução

O CGE recomenda que a população evite transitar por ruas alagadas e não tente atravessar áreas inundadas com correnteza. Também orienta que as pessoas procurem locais seguros, mantenham distância da rede elétrica e não se abriguem debaixo de árvores.

Antes de sair de casa, a recomendação é planejar o trajeto para evitar vias que possam ficar bloqueadas ou provocar congestionamentos.

Para consultar informações sobre o trânsito e possíveis bloqueios, é possível acessar os canais da Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) ou ligar para o telefone 156.

192: Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

156: Atendimento da Prefeitura de São Paulo, incluindo reclamações e dúvidas sobre serviços municipais.

articles.title: Homem morre após cair de motocicleta e ser atropelado em Sumaré | G1
articles.standfirst: Condutor da motocicleta trafegava na marginal, quando, por motivos a serem esclarecidos, caiu do veículo. Na sequência, vítima foi atropelada por um carro. Morte foi constatada no local.
articles.summary: Condutor da motocicleta trafegava na marginal, quando, por motivos a serem esclarecidos, caiu do veículo. Na sequência, vítima foi atropelada. Morte foi constatada no local.
articles.body:
Um homem morreu na manhã deste domingo (15) após cair da motocicleta e ser atropelado por um carro, no km 113 da marginal da Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), sentido capital, em Sumaré (SP). A identificação da vítima não foi informada.

Segundo o Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO) da concessionária Motiva AutoBAn, o condutor da motocicleta trafegava na marginal, quando, por motivos a serem esclarecidos, caiu do veículo. Na sequência, o automóvel, sem tempo hábil de frear ou desviar, atropelou o motociclista .

O motociclista morreu no local do acidente. Já o motorista do carro não sofreu ferimentos.

Homem morre após cair de motocicleta e ser atropelado em Sumaré — Foto: Reprodução

Equipes da concessionária foram mobilizadas para prestar socorro às vítimas, realizar a sinalização e orientar os motoristas.

No início da tarde deste domingo, por volta das 12h30, a ocorrência foi encerrada. O corpo da vítima e os veículos foram removidos, e os trabalhos de perícia foram concluídos.

Homem morre após cair de motocicleta e ser atropelado por carro em Sumaré — Foto: Artesp/CCM

articles.title: Chuva provoca estragos na Grande BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal atingiu Belo Horizonte e outras cidades da Região Metropolitana neste domingo (15). As ocorrências estão relacionadas à queda de árvore, a destelhamentos e a alagamentos.
articles.summary: Temporal atingiu Belo Horizonte e outras cidades da Região Metropolitana neste domingo (15). As ocorrências estão relacionadas à queda de árvore, a destelhamentos e a alagamentos.
articles.body:
BH registra chuva forte e granizo nesta tarde de domingo — Foto: Reprodução/CBMMG

A forte chuva que atingiu Belo Horizonte e cidades da Região Metropolitana, na tarde deste domingo (15), provocou alagamentos, quedas de árvores, destelhamentos e danos a imóveis. Em Nova Lima , uma família ficou presa dentro de casa depois que o vento arrancou completamente o telhado da residência. Em Contagem , uma árvore de aproximadamente 10 metros caiu sobre uma casa.

Na capital mineira, a Defesa Civil recebeu sete chamados entre 13h25 e 15h35. Foram três registros de danos a edificações, dois destelhamentos provocados por vendaval, um deslizamento de encosta e um desabamento de muro.

Ainda segundo o órgão, a Região Leste concentrou o maior número de ocorrências, com três registros, seguida pela Pampulha, com dois. Barreiro e Norte tiveram um chamado cada.

Na Savassi, Região Centro-Sul de BH, uma árvore de grande porte caiu sobre um carro que estava estacionado na Rua Pernambuco. Militares do Corpo de Bombeiros realizaram o corte da árvore para liberar a via.

Em Nova Lima, na Grande BH, uma família ficou presa dentro de casa depois que a chuva e as ventania arrancaram o telhado de um imóvel no bairro Nossa Senhora de Fátima. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, parte das telhas caiu e bloqueou as entradas e saídas da residência, o que impediu os moradores de deixar a casa.

Outra parte da estrutura foi arremessada contra a rede elétrica da rua, provocando risco de queda de materiais sobre pedestres e de acidentes envolvendo a fiação.

De acordo com a Prefeitura de Nova Lima, em duas horas, o município registrou 18 milímetros de chuva e rajadas de vento de até 41 km/h. Não houve vítimas, nem feridos.

Em Contagem, a Defesa Civil recebeu nove chamados relacionados à chuva deste domingo. A cidade registrou alagamentos em quatro regiões. No total, foram oito ocorrências, metade delas na Região Sede.

Uma árvore de aproximadamente 10 metros de altura caiu sobre uma residência na Alameda das Acácias, na Granja Ouro Branco. Outra queda de árvore foi registrada na Estrada Chico Mendes, no bairro Solar Madeira.

articles.title: 'Fiz o que sabia primeiro': estudantes relatam estratégias para Enem | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos relataram que priorizaram disciplinas com maior afinidade para economizar tempo e deixar os conteúdos mais difíceis para o final da prova.
articles.summary: Candidatos relataram que priorizaram disciplinas com maior afinidade para economizar tempo e deixar os conteúdos mais difíceis para o final da prova.
articles.body:
No segundo dia de provas do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, muitos candidatos saíram dos locais de aplicação com a sensação de que administrar o tempo foi tão importante quanto dominar os conteúdos. Entre as estratégias mais citadas pelos estudantes estava começar pelas questões consideradas mais fáceis ou pelas disciplinas com maior afinidade .

Neste domingo (15), os candidatos precisaram administrar o tempo entre 90 questões de Matemática e Ciências da Natureza.

A estudante Cindy Anne Mesquita de Araújo, de 17 anos, contou que decidiu iniciar a prova pelas questões de Biologia, disciplina com a qual tem mais familiaridade.

Segundo ela, a estratégia ajudou a ganhar tempo para se dedicar aos conteúdos em que tem mais dificuldade.

"O que eu tenho mais afinidade é biologia. Eu fiz biologia muito rápido. Sobrou muito tempo para eu conseguir fazer as outras questões que eu tinha mais dificuldade. Então eu fiquei muito feliz com isso", relatou.

'Fiz o que sabia primeiro': estudantes relatam estratégias para o 2º dia do Enem — Foto: Vitória Luna

Cindy afirmou que a preparação antecipada também foi decisiva. A estudante disse que reconheceu questões semelhantes às trabalhadas durante os estudos.

"Eu já fui folheando, eu já sabia as respostas muito rápido. Eu já marquei logo e aí eu fui para as que eu não sabia", contou.

A candidata pretende cursar psicologia ou medicina, com eventual especialização em psiquiatria.

'Fiz o que sabia primeiro': estudantes relatam estratégias para o 2º dia do Enem — Foto: Juliana Cristina/g1

A estudante Layza Maria, de 18 anos, que fez o Enem pela terceira vez, também apostou em uma estratégia semelhante. Segundo ela, a prioridade foi responder primeiro às questões cuja resolução parecia mais clara.

"Eu usei a estratégia mais simples, que é a gente fazer as questões que a gente entende, que a gente sabe o que pode fazer", explicou.

Para a candidata, que pretende cursar direito, o segundo dia foi mais difícil do que as edições anteriores do exame.

"Os anos anteriores, as provas foram mais fáceis, os textos foram diferentes, os cálculos também", avaliou.

Apesar da percepção de maior dificuldade, Layza Maria, saiu da prova com expectativa positiva em relação ao resultado.

"Eu acho que sai uma nota boa, não sei se o suficiente para o que eu quero. Mas acho que sai, por conta do meu esforço", afirmou.

Candidatos no Ceti Professor José Pacífico de Moura Neto, em Teresina, após liberação no 2º dia de provas — Foto: Yngridy Vieira/g1

No Piauí, 120,8 mil pessoas estão inscritas no Enem 2026. Segundo a Secretaria de Estado da Educação do Piauí (Seduc), as provas são realizadas em 49 municípios.

No primeiro dia, os participantes responderam questões de Linguagens, Códigos e suas Tecnologias, Redação e Ciências Humanas e suas Tecnologias.

Neste segundo dia de aplicação, os candidatos fazem provas de Ciências da Natureza e suas Tecnologias e Matemática e suas Tecnologias. A aplicação começou às 13h30 e termina às 18h30, pelo horário de Brasília.

articles.summary: São mais de 1.055 mil vagas de emprego na indústria, comércio e serviço da região; Santa Bárbara d'Oeste concentra a maior parte das oportunidades.
articles.body:
Carteira de trabalho — Foto: Divulgação / PMMC

Cinco cidades da região de Piracicaba (SP) reúnem 1.055 vagas de emprego abertas a partir desta segunda-feira (16). As oportunidades são oferecidas pelos serviços municipais de apoio ao trabalhador.

Há emprego nas áreas de indústria, comércio e serviços , além de estágios em diferentes setores. Confira os destaques abaixo:

👷 Das 157 vagas disponíveis em Cosmópolis, 32 são para Auxiliar de produção;

🔷 Em Limeira, há oportunidades para Azulejista;

🧱 O PAT de Piracicaba oferece vagas para Pedreiro e para Servente de obras;

🛠️ Em Santa Bárbara d'Oeste, são 110 oportunidades, também para Auxiliar de produção;

🧑‍⚕️ Em São Pedro, há processo seletivo para a função de Técnico (a) de Enfermagem;

Clique na cidade de interesse para ver a lista completa:

O Centro de Referência ao Trabalhador de Cosmópolis (CRTC) reúne 157 vagas de emprego em 43 cargos. A unidade fica na Rua Otto Herbst, no Centro.

Quem não é cadastrado precisa ir ao local com as versões originais do CPF, RG, título de eleitor, carteira de trabalho (física ou digital), comprovante de escolaridade e cursos realizados, além do comprovante de endereço.

Já quem tem cadastro pode enviar o currículo pelo e-mail crtc@cosmopolis.sp.gov.br,mcom a vaga de interesse no assunto do e-mail.

A lista completa de vagas e os detalhes podem ser consultados pelo site do CRTC .

O Posto de Atendimento ao Trabalhador (PAT) de Limeira está com 34 oportunidades de trabalho disponíveis em 26 funções .

Os interessados devem se cadastrar no PAT na aba, “ cadastro de currículos ”, pelo site . O PAT de Limeira funciona das 9h às 16h, de segunda a sexta-feira.

Piracicaba tem 44 vagas disponíveis em 37 cargos. Os interessados devem enviar um e-mail para entrevistacatpiracicaba@gmail.com e mencionar qual é o cargo de interesse. O Centro de Atendimento ao Trabalhador (CAT) abre de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h30 às 16h30.

É necessário anexar RG e CPF, além dos comprovantes dos requisitos exigidos pelo contratante. A lista completa de vagas e os detalhes podem ser consultados no Painel de Vagas .

O Desenvolve Santa Bárbara d'Oeste reúne 810 vagas de emprego em 155 funções nesta semana. Os candidatos devem enviar e-mail para empregos@santabarbara.sp.gov.br com nome completo, CPF, RG e currículo. É preciso colocar o nome da vaga de interesse no assunto do e-mail.

Também é possível se candidatar presencialmente na unidade, na Rua do Ósmio, 975, na Villa Multimall.

No atendimento presencial, o trabalhador deve levar RG, CPF e a Carteira de Trabalho. O atendimento é de terça a sexta-feira, das 10h às 22h, e aos sábados, das 10h às 16h.

A lista completa de vagas e os detalhes podem ser consultados pelo site .

O Poupatempo São Pedro abre de segunda a sexta-feira, das 9h às 17h, e aos sábados, das 9h às 13h. O prédio fica na Avenida dos Imigrantes, 688, no Vale do Sol.

É possível entrar em contato com o PAT São Pedro pelo telefone (19) 3481-9392 ou pelo e-mail patsaopedro@sde.sp.gov.br .

A lista completa e o detalhes podem ser consultados pelo site do PAT São Pedro .

articles.title: Caminhonete é arrastada em enchente e fica com a carroceria para cima | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo ficou preso em bueiro na principal avenida da cidade. Por causa do grande volume de chuva, as ruas ficaram alagadas.
articles.summary: Veículo ficou preso em bueiro na principal avenida da cidade. Por causa do grande volume de chuva, as ruas ficaram alagadas.
articles.body:
Uma tempestade atingiu a cidade de Guaraí na tarde deste domingo (15). As ruas ficaram alagadas e carros foram arrastados pela enchente. Em um vídeo publicado pelo morador Railton Noleto, é possível ver uma caminhonete presa em bueiro com a carroceiria para cima.

A chuva forte começou por volta das 15h40. A avenida Bernardo Sayão, que fica no centro da cidade, foi uma das mais afetadas. Em um comércio, foi necessário fazer uma barricada para evitar que a água entrasse.

A Defesa Civil informou que acompanha a situação da cidade e está com ocorrências em andamento.

Caminhonete fica presa em bueiro após ser arrastada durante enchente em Guaraí — Foto: Cedidas/Railton Noleto

A previsão é que a chuva continue durante a noite deste domingo, com muitas nuvens e trovoadas. Na segunda-feira (16), há possibilidade de pancadas de chuva durante todo o dia. A temperatura máxima será de 28 graus e mínima de 23.

O Tocantins está com alerta de tempestade para esta segunda-feira, em todo o território do estado. Nesse período, o volume de chuva pode chegar a 50 milímetros por dia, além de ventos fortes entre 40 e 60 quilômetros por hora.

Em caso de rajadas de vento não se abrigue debaixo de árvores, pois há leve risco de queda e descargas elétricas

articles.title: Enem reúne gerações que buscam na educação chance de mudar de vida | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato de 68 anos busca uma vaga na faculdade. Em outra história, dois primos veem no Enem a chance de realizar o sonho dos pais de chegar ao ensino superior, em Campo Grande.
articles.summary: Conheça as histórias de superação no Enem MS, desde o idoso de 68 anos que sonha com a faculdade até jovens que buscam realizar os desejos de seus pais.
articles.body:
O Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) reúne, neste domingo (15), candidatos com diferentes idades, trajetórias e objetivos em Mato Grosso do Sul. Assista ao vídeo acima.

Na Universidade Católica Dom Bosco (UCDB), um dos locais de prova em Campo Grande , histórias de quem decidiu voltar a estudar mostram que a busca por uma vaga no ensino superior não tem idade certa. Há quem tenha esperado anos para tentar e quem encontre na família a motivação para seguir esse caminho.

Entre os candidatos estão Fábio Joaquim dos Santos, de 68 anos, que pretende cursar Administração, e Enildo Bezerra, de 57, que vê nos estudos uma oportunidade de começar uma nova etapa.

Já o estudante Paulo Henrique Souza, de 31 anos, e a prima Ana Luiza Souza, de 19, têm nos pais a principal inspiração: eles querem aproveitar as oportunidades de estudo que a família não teve no passado.

Candidato de 68 anos do Enem 2026 — Foto: Emilenne Queiroz

Aos 68 anos, Fábio Joaquim dos Santos chegou ao local de prova para tentar uma vaga no ensino superior. Após concluir o ensino médio em 2011, ele continuou estudando por conta própria e decidiu participar do Enem para buscar uma oportunidade de melhorar de vida.

O curso de Administração é o principal objetivo do candidato. Ele conta que também tem interesse pela área do Direito e que mantém os estudos com materiais que adquiriu ao longo do tempo.

O candidato sabe que a aprovação representaria a realização de um sonho. Mesmo assim, mantém a disposição de continuar tentando. "A gente vai à luta ver se consegue", disse.

Candidato de 57 anos do Enem 2026 sonha em cursar psicologia. — Foto: Emilenne Queiroz

Aos 57 anos, Enildo Bezerra decidiu voltar a estudar para iniciar uma nova etapa da vida. Para ele, o Enem representa a oportunidade de adquirir conhecimentos, cuidar da saúde mental e encontrar novos objetivos.

O candidato conta que a rotina de trabalho e as responsabilidades familiares limitaram o tempo de preparação durante o ano. Ainda assim, conseguiu estudar e saiu satisfeito com o primeiro dia de prova, principalmente com a redação.

"Quando a gente chega numa idade mais avançada, acha que está tudo parando. É você se reinventar", explicou.

Para o futuro, Enildo considera cursar Psicologia ou Farmácia. Ele acredita que voltar a estudar ajuda a renovar a mente e abre caminhos para novos conhecimentos.

Paulo Henrique e Ana Luiza são primos e vão fizeram o Enem 2026 — Foto: Emilenne Queiroz

Paulo Henrique Souza, de 31 anos, participa do Enem pela segunda vez. Neste ano, ele chegou à prova com a expectativa de ter um desempenho melhor e afirma que se preparou mais.

A decisão de buscar uma vaga na faculdade tem relação com a história da família. Os pais de Paulo não tiveram a oportunidade de estudar, e essa realidade se tornou uma motivação para que ele tentasse seguir um caminho diferente.

‘Meus pais me apoiam e quero dar orgulho para eles. Seu eu conseguir, vai ser ótimo”

Ele vê no exame uma oportunidade de conquistar um objetivo pessoal e ampliar as possibilidades de formação.

A prima de Paulo, Ana Luiza Souza, de 19 anos, também encontra na família a principal motivação para fazer o Enem. Ela conta que os pais e outros familiares não tiveram acesso à educação como gostariam, e que isso fortalece sua vontade de continuar estudando.

"Meus pais. Meus pais e todo mundo da minha família", respondeu ao ser questionada sobre o que a motiva a fazer a prova.

Ana Luiza conta que ficou nervosa no primeiro dia e teve dificuldade para organizar as ideias durante a redação. Mesmo assim, acredita que conseguiu alcançar um resultado dentro do esperado. “Eles nunca fizeram uma prova, não terminaram o ensino fundamental. Nem internet minha família tinha", conta.

Para este domingo, a estudante afirma que se preparou e espera fazer uma prova melhor. A expectativa é conquistar uma vaga no ensino superior e dar continuidade a um caminho que, segundo ela, representa uma oportunidade para toda a família.

articles.title: Darrell Dai, a robot research engineer at Nvidia resigns; complains to Nvidia board: You did not hear engineers working in the company on Jensen Huang, we also have a 'story to tell'
articles.summary: Nvidia robotics research engineer Darrell Dai has announced his resignation from the company, expressing disappointment over the lack of communication
articles.body: Nvidia robotics research engineer Darrell Dai has announced his resignation from the company, expressing disappointment over the lack of communication with engineers following Jensen Huang’s departure amid allegations and an ongoing investigation. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Darrell Dai said he admired Jensen Huang’s vision and the engineering culture he built, but felt that employees’ perspectives had not been heard on a decision affecting the company’s future. “I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny,” Dai said, adding “What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it”.Here’s the post shared by Nvidia robot research engineer"I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.That is why this has been so disappointing.I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.These are my personal views."Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: 28 years after Wendy Hudakoc vanished in Naples, Florida, her sister is still searching for answers
articles.summary: Wendy Hudakoc vanished from Naples, Florida, in November 1998. The Collier County Sheriff’s Office continues to investigate her case.
articles.body: In the 1990s, sisters Sharlene and Wendy Hudakoc moved from Canada to Florida. “The United States in general was a big difference, and then coming to Florida, that was even that much more of a difference,” Sharlene Boyatt told “Dateline.” “It was just a whole ‘nother world down here.” Sharlene says they were typical teenagers, “hanging out with friends, going to the beach.” Just two years apart, the sisters fought “like sisters, but at the same time, we hung out, too.” Sharlene remembers her 14-year-old sister as full of life. “She was just always out for the adventure. Nothing really scared her,” she said. “She was ready to take on pretty much everything head-on.” The sisters lived in Naples, Florida, with their mom and stepdad. On the weekend of Nov. 14, 1998, their parents went out of town. “They had some friends of theirs come and spend the weekend over with us, just because even at 16 and 14, we were still too young to be home alone,” Sharlene explained. On the evening of Saturday, Nov. 14, Sharlene had a friend over to spend the night. “[Wendy] had planned to go to a friend’s party that night,” Sharlene said. After taking a phone call, Wendy asked if they wanted to join her. “I said, ‘No way. You can go. We’re staying in watching movies.’” Wendy later snuck out of the house to attend the party. The next morning, Sunday, Nov. 15, Sharlene went to Wendy’s room. “She wasn’t there. The window was still open. There was a towel laid over the windowsill, and a candle was still lit on the outside on the ground by her window, so she could kinda, like, see to get back in the house,” Sharlene said. “Her room was hot and humid. I remember that. And it was — she wasn’t there.” Sharlene didn’t panic at first. “I kinda figured she maybe was still at her friend’s house, she didn’t get a ride home. I wasn’t sure,” she said. Then she remembered Wendy had taken their stepdad’s pager with her the night before. “I started paging her, ‘cause I didn’t know what time my parents were gonna be back,” Sharlene recalled. “I started paging her and paging her and paging her and paging her, and after a couple of hours, I was like, ‘OK, something is wrong.’” So Sharlene called their parents, who were checking out of their hotel on the east coast of Florida. “They were standing at the front desk. And when I called the front desk, they handed the phone right to my parents,” she said. “And I had to tell them that Wendy never came home.” Her parents immediately drove to Naples. When they arrived, they began making calls. “They called the police. They started calling all of her friends,” Sharlene said. “We had a phone book at the house with all of our friends’ names and phone numbers in it, and of course, my parents start calling every single one of them wanting to know if anybody’s seen her, if they know anything.” Looking back on those early days following Wendy’s disappearance, Sharlene remembers it being chaotic. “I don’t remember a whole lot about it. I remember driving around with my mom,” she said. “I remember it was either that night or the following evening, we were sitting in front of the TV, and I remember getting up and saying, ‘I’m never going to see my sister again.’” Sharlene says she couldn’t explain the feeling. “It was just one of those gut feelings, and it sucks that it’s the one that came true,” she said. As the family began piecing together Wendy’s movements that night, they learned she reportedly left the party with the same man who brought her there. According to Sharlene, Wendy was last seen with the man around 2:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 15, 1998. “All of her friends saw her leave with this guy.” Sharlene says their stepdad and uncle began trying to identify the person Wendy’s friends said she left the party with. “They started doing their own investigation, basically,” she said. “They had gone and talked to the kids that were at the party that night, and they got the name Ron from them.” According to Sharlene, their stepdad and uncle printed out mug shots of men within a certain age range who had recently been arrested. “They took all of those pictures and brought them back to the kids, and the kids all pointed him out,” she said. Sharlene says the man whose mug shot the partygoers identified was of Ron DePeppo. “Dateline” spoke with investigator Ralph DiFonzo of the Collier County Sheriff’s Office cold case unit, who was assigned Wendy’s case after joining the department about two years ago. He confirmed that the sheriff’s office opened an investigation within 24 hours of her disappearance in 1998. DiFonzo says investigators extensively interviewed people who were at the party where Wendy was last seen in the early morning hours of Nov. 15, 1998. They also interviewed family members, friends and others who might have had information. “That’s a lot of interviews to be conducted,” he said. “That was the majority of the investigation.” He also noted that investigators had no specific area to focus their search on, and no significant evidence was found. DiFonzo confirmed that Wendy was last seen with a man named Ron DePeppo, who was interviewed in 1998. A week to 10 days after Wendy disappeared, DePeppo’s car caught fire. Investigators examined the car afterward but found “nothing of value” to the investigation, according to DiFonzo. No suspects have been named in Wendy’s case. DiFonzo considers DePeppo a person of interest, but emphasized that there are “a lot of people, a lot of parties, a lot of names, a lot of individuals,” and “everyone had to be looked at.” The sheriff’s office has not recently spoken to DePeppo. According to Sharlene, he no longer lives in the area. “Dateline” was unable to locate him for comment. DiFonzo believes Wendy may have been the victim of foul play. Her case was entered into the FBI’s Violent Criminal Apprehension Program (ViCAP). Over the years, investigators have compared Wendy’s case with unidentified remains, but no matches have been found. DiFonzo says investigators have familial DNA on file for identification purposes. Wendy’s case remains open. DiFonzo hopes someone with information will now be willing to come forward. “They may have left something out. They may have been too scared when they were younger,” he said. “I mean, there’s a lot of things that can change over the course of the years, so that would help if somebody had a change of heart.” Nearly three decades later, Sharlene shares that hope. “It’s just that constantly not knowing and living in a state of — of — of not knowing is pretty—. It — it — it causes a lot of anxiety, to say the least,” she said. “It’s not something you can just stop thinking about.” “I graduated high school. I got married. I’ve had children,” Sharlene said. Milestones Wendy never got to experience. “I lost my parent — my mom. I’ve lost grandparents,” she added. “I’ve lost just about everybody. And I would like to not go to my grave not knowing — the way my mom did.” And Sharlene doesn’t just want to learn what happened to Wendy. She wants to bring her home, so she can lay her to rest with their mother, who died in 2013. “I want to just let her be with my mom.” Authorities continue to seek information about Wendy’s disappearance. In 1998, Wendy was 5’6” and 130 lbs., and wore braces on her teeth. She had light brown hair and hazel eyes, a scar on her left hand and a birthmark on the back of her neck. In 2020, around the 22nd anniversary of Wendy’s disappearance, the CCSO shared an age-progression image created by the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children. The image depicts what Wendy might have looked like at age 36. She would be 42 years old today. If you have any information about Wendy’s disappearance, please contact the Collier County Sheriff’s Office at 239-252-9300. You can also submit an anonymous tip with the Southwest Florida Crime Stoppers at 1-800-780-TIPS (8477) or online. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: 20- to 30-foot waves pound the West Coast as storms continue
articles.summary: Waves 20 to 30 feet high are expected in some areas Sunday.
articles.body:
Much of the West Coast continues to face hazardous coastal conditions on Sunday, including 20- to 30-foot waves slamming waterfront communities.

Coastal impacts are expected Sunday along nearly the entire length of the West Coast, from Southern California to the Northwest states, as a series of storms fuel widespread dangerous rough surf.

The latest storm system has moved into the Pacific Northwest, bringing another round of rain and mountain snow from Northern California to Washington and Oregon.

But the primary concern on Sunday will be focused on the persistent rough surf and large waves across much of the West Coast amid back-to-back storms.

High surf alerts remained in effect on Sunday along much of the West Coast.

Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet in height are expected to continue along the Northern California, Oregon and Washington coasts before easing on Monday.

The large waves will create hazardous conditions along the coast, with waves inundating beaches and potentially bringing significant beach erosion and damage.

Periods of rain along the Pacific Northwest Coast will spread inland across the Intermountain West and Northern California.

Some of the highest elevations of the Cascade Mountains could see some snow as well.

Meanwhile, a new system is expected to bring more unsettled weather to the Pacific Northwest Coast by early Wednesday.

Widespread showers and storms are forecast across southeastern Texas on Sunday, with isolated downpours possible.

Localized flash flooding could develop where the heaviest rain moves through, including metropolitan Houston, Galveston and Freeport.

Rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches are forecast across the region, with isolated amounts up to 4 inches possible through Sunday night.

Storms in southeast Texas are expected to bring heavy rain, with 1 to 2 inches possible across most of the region and some areas receiving 4 to 6 inches.

The weather system hitting southeast Texas is also bringing windy conditions along the coast, with gusts of up to 40 mph possible, leading authorities to warn residents about the potential of falling tree limbs and scattered power outages.

articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
articles.summary: Eight arrests made in connection with an attempted arson, which Tallinn says was ordered by Russian intelligence.
articles.body:
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia, after an attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blames on Moscow.

The foreign minister made the announcement on Sunday, after eight people were detained overnight in connection with an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.

Estonian authorities said the attacks had been ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna wrote on X, “Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences. Attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will not go unanswered.

“Closing the border crossings will reduce Russia’s ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia and strengthen our efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention.”

He did not specify how long the border closure would last.

A Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman told state news agency TASS that the plans were “yet another bout of aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia.”

Latvia’s Interior Minister Janis Dombrava thanked Estonia’s Internal Security Service on X, saying that several “Latvian citizens and non-citizens” were arrested.

“Since the collapse of the USSR, there have been people among us who are willing to commit serious crimes in Russia’s interests. We will continue our work to ensure that such people cannot endanger the lives of those who love Latvia and want to live in safety,” Dombrava wrote.

Estonia, a European Union and NATO member state and a strong ally of Ukraine , currently has three open border crossings with Russia at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula.

Marko Mihkelson, chairman of the Estonian Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, told Al Jazeera that the arrests demonstrated that Estonia was “prepared to respond swiftly to such attacks.”

“It is essential that Russia’s state-sponsored campaign of terror does not remain merely a matter of diplomatic protests, either in Estonia or among our allies elsewhere,” Mihkelson said.

“Russia is waging a shadow war to divide Europe and undermine support for Ukraine. European countries must respond with asymmetric measures of their own. Closing borders with Russia is one such measure.”

articles.title: An Australian railway enthusiast spent 13 years building a miniature version of a 315-kilometre Adelaide-to-Serviceton rail route inside his backyard shed, complete with 50 metres of track over three levels
articles.summary: The Adelaide-to-Bridgewater passenger service ended in 1987. In Peter Michalak’s backyard shed, the train still makes the journey.
articles.body: The Adelaide-to-Bridgewater passenger service ended in 1987. In Peter Michalak’s backyard shed, the train still makes the journey. It passes the station, the old mill and a tree-covered hillside, moving through a miniature version of South Australia where some journeys never stopped.For 13 years, Michalak has been building the Hills Line, an HO-scale, i.e. 1:87, railway recreating the 315-kilometre corridor between Adelaide and Serviceton, just across the Victorian border. About 50 metres of mainline track loops through three levels, passing stations, freight yards and hills.Bridgewater is the heart of the project. Passenger trains once carried people from Adelaide into the Adelaide Hills, but services beyond Belair were withdrawn in 1987. Patronage had fallen, particularly after the South Eastern Freeway offered a faster route into the city. Today, passenger trains terminate at Belair. In Michalak’s version of events, the service to Bridgewater never disappeared.“I grew up catching SteamRanger trains to Bridgewater as a kid in the school holidays,” he told the ABC. “I had a lot of memories of going up there, and I had to create it.” Bridgewater was the first station he built, originally as a portable model for exhibitions. It has since become the centrepiece of a much larger railway. “Bridgewater, in this reality, still has passenger train services to it,” he said.The Adelaide-to-Melbourne route was once part of a broad-gauge network, with the lines meeting at Serviceton in 1887. In 1995, the interstate corridor was converted to standard gauge. Serviceton’s two-storey brick station, built in 1888, was a border hub with customs offices and a place for South Australian and Victorian train crews to change over. Michalak has left space for it, although its full model is still a work in progress.The railway is not a literal miniature map of 315 kilometres. Michalak calls it “selectively compressed”: the trains are HO scale, but distances, platforms and infrastructure have been shortened to fit the space. A 70-wagon freight train, for instance, becomes a 10-wagon one. He describes himself as a “proto freelancer”, taking recognisable elements of the real railway and recreating a version that works within the shed. Mile End, once a huge rail yard, is represented by three tracks.The layout also includes Pinnaroo, Tailem Bend, Mount Lofty and a branch to Port Adelaide, where a miniature version of the heritage Hart’s Mill stands beside the tracks. Buildings are made by hand, while the roads carry period cars, including a green VB Commodore matching the family car Michalak remembers from childhood. Tiny signs and a Country Fire Service truck at a level crossing placed the railway in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Trees around Bridgewater are fashioned from sedum, a garden plant.Some trains can be bought ready-made. Others, particularly those unique to South Australia, have to be built from scratch. That includes the Redhen railcars, locally built passenger trains that served Adelaide from the 1950s until 1996. Michalak’s brother, Nick, prepares computer-aided design drawings, while Michalak 3D-prints components for engines and carriages. He still cuts, folds and solders brass by hand, a process that comes with burnt fingers and a fair amount of swearing.Railway history runs through Michalak’s family. His grandfather began working as a porter at Tailem Bend station, and Michalak received his first electric train set when he was three. Local history groups have helped him find photographs and records missing from museums. His brother is building Blackwood station, while a friend and former railway controller has drawn up train-control graphs for operating sessions, compressing a 12-hour shift into about two and a half hours.Beyond the shed, Michalak is vice-president of SteamRanger Heritage Railway, which operates tourist trains between Mount Barker and Victor Harbor. In 2026, he documented its history in a 116-page book illustrated with more than 200 images and accounts from volunteers.The Hills Line began in 2013 as a portable model of Bridgewater. By 2016, Michalak and his wife had decided to turn it into a permanent home layout. It has since outgrown its original purpose and is now too large to travel. He estimates it could take another decade to finish. Adelaide station is being recreated as it looked in the late 1980s, complete with its distinctive orange platform chairs. Serviceton, still partly represented by a cardboard mock-up, is waiting its turn.There is a satisfaction in watching a train pass through a place reconstructed down to its signage and station furniture. But this is not a museum display meant only to be peered into. Signals, timetables and train movements are meant to be used. “It’s a very social part of it all,” Michalak told ABC. “It’s built to use.”For now, Bridgewater still has its trains. And in this small, carefully assembled version of South Australia, the past has somewhere to go.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Prince Harry in Ukraine meeting Invictus 2027 hopefuls
articles.summary: British royal says he’s ‘taken a risk’ in his fourth surprise visit to Ukraine since 2022 to meet wounded veterans.
articles.body:
Britain’s Prince Harry has met wounded veterans and medics in Ukraine during a surprise visit.

The royal family member attended Ukraine’s National Invictus Games and a conference for medics in the western city of Lviv on Saturday. It was organised by Superhumans, a clinic that specialises in the rehabilitation of war-wounded.

“Every single time I come back to Ukraine, I feel welcome, I feel warmth,” Harry said, adding that he’d “taken a risk to come here”.

Ukraine has about 1.4 million combat veterans, more than 10 percent of whom have disabilities.

“You’re going to win the war,” the 42-year-old British royal said during his fourth trip to the country since the start of the conflict with Russia in 2022.

The prince watched wheelchair rugby players competing for a place in Ukraine’s team for next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham in England.

Around 500 people have registered to compete to qualify for the 60-member squad – the largest ever team – that Ukraine is planning to send to the 2027 event.

“You’re going to win the war and then you’re going to be set up for success,” he said.

Prince Harry is the founder and patron of the Invictus Games Foundation, which he established in 2014 to support wounded, injured and recovering military service personnel and veterans through adaptive sports, e-sports and recovery programmes.

“When the war is over and when Ukraine wins, we will be ready to support you in holding an Invictus Games,” Harry told wounded veterans later on Saturday.

At a rugby game, he hugged Valery Odainyk, a contestant at the Invictus Games in Canada last year. The leg amputee is “still an active serviceman” in the Ukrainian forces.

“So when do you find time to train?” Harry asked in surprise.

The 41-year-old Odainyk said he told Harry that his involvement in disability sport “all started and continues with the Invictus Games.”

They feature a mix of adaptive core and winter sports, such as alpine skiing, archery, track and field, cycling, wheelchair basketball, rugby and tennis.

articles.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts confining J&K’s depiction to “scenic beauty, skullcaps that few
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts confining J&K’s depiction to “scenic beauty, skullcaps that few in the Valley actually wear and AK-47s carried under pherans and long beards”, while calling for strengthening indigenous filmmaking.Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday by Kashmir Music Club, run by popular singer Waheed Jeelani.“We have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,” actor Umar Imtiyaz said as he took potshots at Bollywood for dishing out its familiar fare of “skullcaps, long beards and AK-47s under pherans (long, loose-fitting garments worn by Kashmiris in winter)”. Imtiyaz argued that it was time to challenge such stereotypical representations.Echoing the sentiment, filmmaker Ayash Arif called for a focus on regional cinema that blends local concerns with a broader global outlook. He criticised J&K govt’s film policy, arguing it was more of a tourism blueprint aimed at encouraging filmmakers from elsewhere to shoot in the region due to its scenic beauty. What is needed, Arif said, is a roadmap aimed at promoting local productions.The 2022 policy offers several initiatives, including a single-window portal for shooting permissions and subsidies. It recalls the heady 1960s when blockbusters like Kashmir Ki Kali, Jab Jab Phool Khile, Himalay Ki God Mein and Janwar were shot in Srinagar and Gulmarg, followed by some international productions such as The Razor’s Edge in the 1980s.At the seminar, however, many felt the policy does not address requirements back home. “There is a lot for outside filmmakers in the policy but not much for local makers,” Arif said.Director Kapil Matoo, whose recent film Tasrufdar: Djinns of Kashmir won critical acclaim, urged local filmmakers to shed a sense of victimhood and recognise their own potential. “We must have our own industry here and start making films as we have stories of every shade,” Matoo said.Actor-director Mir Sarwar exhorted local artists not to depend on the limited opportunities offered by Doordarshan Srinagar and J&K Academy of Art. “We must help each other rather than wait for roles from filmmakers who come from outside,” Sarwar said. Cinematographer Shafqat Habib felt Kashmiri filmmakers must carve out a distinct identity.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Eleven years after Chris Singleton lost his mother in the Charleston church shooting, a memorial backed by $25 million in fundraising has opened; he now has a place to visit when he wants to remember her
articles.summary: A permanent memorial honouring nine Black worshippers murdered in a racist attack at a historic church in Charleston, South Carolina, has opened more than
articles.body: A permanent memorial honouring nine Black worshippers murdered in a racist attack at a historic church in Charleston, South Carolina, has opened more than 11 years after the shooting. Chris Singleton, whose mother was among those killed, said the new site gives him a place to visit whenever he wants to remember her. The Emanuel Nine Memorial was officially opened on Saturday, 14 November 2026, beside the historic Mother Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church. The project followed a major fundraising campaign that raised approximately $25 million (£19 million), according to the Associated Press (AP).Families of the victims, survivors and community leaders attended the dedication and ribbon-cutting ceremony. Local broadcaster Live 5 News reported that people gathered to mark the opening of the memorial. The shooting took place on 17 June 2015, when a white supremacist opened fire during a Bible study session at the church. Nine people were killed: State Senator and Reverend Clementa Pinckney, Reverend Sharonda Coleman-Singleton, Cynthia Graham Hurd, Reverend Daniel Simmons, Reverend DePayne Middleton-Doctor, Myra Quarles Thompson, Ethel Lee Lance, Susie Jackson and Tywanza Sanders. Five others survived. The memorial honours those who died and provides a place for visitors to remember the victims and learn about the attack.A place of quiet reflectionThe memorial was designed to offer a peaceful place for remembrance and reflection. Its layout focuses on peace, reconciliation and hope while creating a quiet space in downtown Charleston. According to Live 5 News, the site features two large curved marble benches arranged around a central fountain. The benches allow visitors to sit and reflect, while the fountain carries the names of the nine victims. The design also includes a Cross of Hope, which represents forgiveness and redemption. It was created by Michael Arad, a partner at Handel Architects who also designed the National September 11 Memorial in New York City. The Associated Press reported that the memorial's marble courtyard was designed to encourage visitors to focus on the people who lost their lives rather than only the circumstances of their deaths. A Survivors' Garden is also planned as part of the wider project.For Chris Singleton, the opening has a personal meaning. His mother, Reverend Sharonda Coleman-Singleton, was among those killed in the 2015 shooting. Singleton was 18 at the time and has since become a motivational speaker and author. Speaking to Live 5 News, he explained why having a permanent place to remember his mother matters. "So, we don’t have a burial site for her. But this will be somewhere I can find solace and go through my emotions when I need to have that moment with my mom," Singleton said. According to Live 5 News, his mother's ashes were placed in the ocean in Jamaica. The new memorial gives him and other relatives a place to remember their loved ones.Honouring resilience over griefThe dedication ceremony also recognised the strength shown by the victims' families, survivors and the wider Charleston community since the attack. The Associated Press reported that speakers focused on resilience and the importance of keeping the victims' memories alive. William Dudley Hurd, whose sister Cynthia Graham Hurd was among those killed, spoke about the meaning of remembrance during the dedication. His message reflected the belief that the hatred behind the attack had not destroyed the love shared by the families and community."This isn't just about grief. This is about resilience. They took away our loved ones, but they could not take away the love," Hurd said, according to the AP report. Other speakers also highlighted the importance of reconciliation and challenging racist beliefs. Community leaders hope the memorial will become an educational destination, attracting visitors who want to learn about the shooting and the history of Mother Emanuel AME Church. Founded in 1818, the church has a long history in Charleston's Black community. According to the Associated Press, it became an important centre for civil rights activity, with Reverend Martin Luther King Jr. and other leaders speaking there.The legacy of fundraisingThe memorial required years of planning and a major fundraising effort. The Mother Emanuel Memorial Foundation was established in 2017 to oversee the project and raise money for its construction and long-term upkeep. According to the Associated Press and Live 5 News, the campaign raised approximately $25 million. Donations came from individuals, foundations, companies and public sources, including the state of South Carolina and the city of Charleston. Around $5 million of the total has been set aside as a permanent endowment to cover future maintenance costs. Organisers say this will help ensure the memorial remains in good condition without placing an ongoing financial burden on the church congregation. The funding covers the memorial's design and construction, along with the long-term costs of maintaining the site. The endowment is intended to protect the project for future generations. Local officials told Live 5 News that long-term funding was an important part of creating a lasting tribute. The foundation also plans to continue educational and community activities linked to the memorial.Healing and enduring impactThe opening marks another important moment in Charleston's efforts to remember the 2015 attack and support the families affected by it. The murders prompted widespread discussions across the United States about racism, gun violence and Confederate symbols. In the weeks after the shooting, South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley called for the Confederate battle flag to be removed from the State House grounds in Columbia. The flag was taken down in July 2015 following public pressure. The attack also brought national attention to racial violence and the experiences of Black communities. Charleston's response, particularly the calls for forgiveness and unity from victims' families and church members, became an important part of the aftermath. More than a decade later, the Emanuel Nine Memorial provides a permanent place to remember those who died and recognise the people who survived. It also gives younger generations an opportunity to learn about the attack and the history of the church. For Singleton and other relatives, the site offers a place to sit quietly and remember the people they lost. The memorial now stands beside Mother Emanuel AME Church as a lasting tribute to the nine victims and the community they left behind.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Thousands of US flights cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
articles.summary: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.
articles.body:
Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday as the US air-traffic control system continued to recover from a technical failure that led to a rare national ground stop.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said normal operations may not be restored until Monday.

"We have airplanes and crews that are out of position, so it takes a little bit of time," he told the BBC's US partner CBS. More than 5,000 flights were delayed and 2,000 cancelled on Sunday.

President Donald Trump urged Congress on Sunday to approve more money to modernise the air-traffic control system. The grounding of all aircraft scheduled to depart the US on Friday caused chaos at airports across the country.

More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air when the FAA announced at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) that flights would be grounded until further notice. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations.

In the aftermath, 8,500 flights were delayed and another 8,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware.

The stoppage left passengers stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to their gates. Others were stranded in airports, sleeping on the floor and desperately trying to get in touch with their airline. The ground stop also had a knock-on effect on schedules around the world, with some flights out of the UK and Europe cancelled.

The ground stop was lifted after about four and a half hours, but the impacts continued over the weekend.

On Saturday, airlines cancelled more than 5,900 flights and more than 7,000 others were delayed.

Investigators are still working to determine the root cause and who is at fault, but Duffy said the administration decided to ground flights after failures in a key system that allows air traffic controllers and pilots to communicate.

The transport secretary said a computer router installed as part of an upgrade from copper wire to fibre started sending out faulty signals.

He said on Sunday that the router - a piece of equipment which directs traffic across the network - was installed in El Dorado, Arkansas, and "flooded our network".

Duffy said that issues will continue to arise until the US makes major modernising changes to its air control system. The system needs a complete overhaul, he said.

"Let's not lie to each other," he said on NBC's Meet The Press. "We have to make investments into a network that has been neglected for decades."

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump urged US lawmakers to allocate the money, saying "we can get it built quickly and efficiently".

"It will be the BEST SYSTEM anywhere in the World. Much of our current air control system is 50 years old - RIDICULOUS! We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," he said.

Experts say the US uses antiquated technology for flight communications.

Aviation analyst Miles O'Brien described the US system as "a house that's about to be condemned".

He told the BBC: "I think most of us could look at this and go 'this is a system in the United States that we have allowed to decay'. It is worse than a fixer-upper."

articles.title: A Texas husband and wife took money for more than 24 custom-home projects but left families with unfinished houses; a court ordered them to pay $2.79 million
articles.summary: A Texas couple who collected millions of dollars from families seeking custom-built homes has been sentenced after leaving dozens of construction projects
articles.body: A Texas couple who collected millions of dollars from families seeking custom-built homes has been sentenced after leaving dozens of construction projects unfinished. Christopher Judge and his wife, Raquelle Judge, operated through their company, Judge DFW LLC, offering architecture, construction and interior design services that frequently failed to materialise. According to the US Department of Justice, the couple defrauded more than 40 victims across at least 24 projects in North Texas. Their scheme left homeowners facing unfinished properties, financial losses and the difficult task of finding contractors to repair or complete the work.Texas couple sentenced over unfinished custom home projectsThe US Department of Justice announced on September 1, 2026, that Christopher Judge, 35, and Raquelle Judge, 36, had been sentenced for their roles in a years-long fraud conspiracy involving custom-home construction projects. Both had pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud in December 2025.Christopher Judge received 78 months in federal prison, followed by two years of supervised release. His wife was sentenced to one month in prison. The couple was also ordered to pay $2,794,680.73 in restitution to compensate victims for their losses.The Justice Department said the estimated financial damage associated with the scheme was approximately $4.2 million. The case involved homeowners across 6 counties in North Texas who had entered agreements expecting their construction projects to be completed.The sentences followed an investigation into how the couple secured contracts, collected payments and repeatedly failed to deliver the homes and renovations they had promised.How did the construction business attract homeownersAccording to the Justice Department's December 31, 2025, announcement, the Judges operated Judge DFW LLC, a Texas-based company through which they offered custom architecture, construction and interior design services.The business attracted customers by presenting below-market bids for design-and-build projects. Homeowners signed contracts after being offered services that appeared affordable and suited to their requirements.The company began construction on several properties and collected multiple instalment payments from clients. However, the work was frequently left incomplete, with some projects abandoned altogether.Court documents also revealed that Christopher Judge falsely represented himself as a licensed architect. The claim helped establish confidence among customers who believed they were hiring a qualified professional to oversee their homes.The December 2025 Justice Department release said the couple admitted to conspiring to defraud consumers between August 2020 and January 2023.Homeowners discovered serious construction problemsThe consequences extended beyond delays and incomplete buildings. Families who had expected to move into carefully designed homes instead found themselves dealing with defective construction and additional expenses.CBS Texas reported in January 2026, that homeowner Kalie Simmons had been attracted to the Judges' promises of custom designs, renovations and a dream home. She and her parents were looking to update their property when they encountered the company in 2021.The proposals appeared appealing because of the low prices, quick turnaround promises and Christopher Judge's claimed architectural credentials. However, the finished work did not match what customers had been promised.Simmons pointed to problems inside her Euless home, including uneven floors, windows that were not properly aligned and a backsplash that had not been installed as planned. She also discovered that the architectural licence claimed by Christopher Judge did not exist.Families faced substantial financial and personal lossesFor some homeowners, the financial consequences continued long after the construction work stopped.CBS Texas reported that Kristin Newman, 36, had been trying to build her first home when she became one of the victims. She subsequently spent approximately $450,000 attempting to repair unfinished construction work and was living with her parents while selling the property.The additional costs meant that the original building contracts were only part of the financial burden. Homeowners also had to find money for repairs, unfinished work and the practical difficulties of living without a completed residence.The emotional impact was equally significant. Chelle Bish, Simmons' mother, expressed concern that families could be pushed into bankruptcy because of the actions of people they had trusted.Where did the homeowners' payments goOne of the central findings in the case concerned the handling of money collected from customers.According to the Justice Department's December 2025 announcement, the Judges combined victims' instalment payments in the company's main operating account. Individual customers' payments were frequently used to finance unrelated construction projects rather than being reserved for the work for which they had been collected.This meant that money paid towards one home could be used elsewhere in the business, leaving customers dependent on the company continuing to operate and generate funds.CBS Texas reported that prosecutors alleged money collected from homeowners had been used for personal expenses, including luxury purchases and plastic surgery. The Justice Department's September 2026 announcement subsequently placed the estimated losses at approximately $4.2 million.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
