articles.title: In a world first, China’s 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft makes crewed flight
articles.summary: Ushering in a new era in the aviation sector, China has flown the world’s first 10-tonne-class commercial passenger aircraft that operates on
articles.body: Ushering in a new era in the aviation sector, China has flown the world’s first 10-tonne-class commercial passenger aircraft that operates on battery-electric power.Moving from the aviation turbine fuel (ATF) era, China’s CE-25A successfully completed its maiden crewed flight on Saturday. The aircraft carried two pilots and one flight-test engineer during the flight in Binzhou in east China’s Shandong province, China’s state-owned television broadcaster CCTV said.Though Militky MB-E1 (a motor glider) is recognised as the world’s first full-size electric aircraft to fly on battery-electric power with a person on board on Oct 21, 1973, in Austria, China’s CE-25A is the first 19-seater 10-tonne-class battery-electric commercial passenger aircraft. Israel has also developed a prototype of electric aircraft Eviation Alice with a carrying capacity of nine passengers and two crew members but has not taken the project forward.Developed jointly by Chinese state-owned aerospace manufacturer Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC), Chinese battery maker CATL, Shanghai Jiao Tong University and other partners, CE-25A had earlier completed 19 unmanned autonomous flight validations. The Civil Aviation Administration of China has accepted COMAC’s application for a type certificate. articles.title: Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’
articles.summary: ‘If we don’t stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak,’ Africa CDC director says.
articles.body:
Africa’s top public health agency says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is still not under control six months after it was declared.

“If we don’t stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak that the world will have,” Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), told Reuters news agency on Sunday.

Since the outbreak was announced on May 15, more than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been recorded, according to government data.

Kaseya said that more than “80 percent of ‌new cases emerge outside contact lists and over 65 percent of deaths” have occurred in the community outside health centres.

Cases have now been reported in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

“We are all in agreement today to say that this outbreak is still serious, and is ⁠still not under control,” Kaseya said.

The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which can trigger haemorrhagic fever.

It is the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind only the 2014-2016 West African outbreak. That epidemic infected more than 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000.

Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected in the ongoing outbreak, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centres.

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have led to a more rapid spread of the virus than in previous outbreaks.

Kaseya said coordination between DRC and donors remained a problem, calling it “a collective failure”.

Only $1.3bn of the $2.9bn pledged by donors to fight Ebola has been released, according to Kaseya.

“We are not pointing fingers,” he said, adding that Africa CDC was working closely with Kinshasa to ensure money isn’t wasted ‌through ‌duplication and that the DRC was working to digitise the payroll to health workers who “hadn’t been paid for months”.

Containment has been especially difficult because no vaccine or treatment has been developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, which kills about half of the people it infects.

Earlier this month, the World Health Organization (WHO) approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines and said it expected results in early 2027.

“Transmission is slowing in several early epicentres, and clinical trials, including the Tumaini trial and new vaccine candidates, are advancing rapidly”, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote in a post on X.

The WHO said at least 3,000 people have recovered from Ebola virus disease in DRC and returned home.

articles.body: Where is sports betting legal? As of November 2026, sports betting is legal in 39 states and Washington, DC, and online betting is live in 31 of those states plus DC. Eight states allow only in-person betting, and 11 have not legalized sports betting at all. This guide covers the current status of every state, including launch dates, legal betting ages, college betting rules and which major sportsbooks operate where. It also tracks the states closest to legalizing next and explains how prediction markets fit into the picture. Last updated: Nov. 12, 2026. How Many States Have Legal Sports Betting? Sports betting falls into three categories across the US. Here is where every state stands as of November 2026. Wisconsin is the closest to adding online betting. The state legalized tribal mobile betting in April 2026, but apps are not yet live. Legal Sports Betting States Quick Reference How Sports Betting Became Legal in the US For decades, the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act of 1992 (PASPA) barred most states from authorizing sports betting. Nevada was exempt. Delaware, Montana and Oregon kept limited carve-outs for older lottery-style products. New Jersey challenged the law, and on May 14, 2018, the US Supreme Court ruled in Murphy v. NCAA that PASPA was unconstitutional. The decision left each state free to set its own rules, and Delaware took the first legal single-game bet outside Nevada weeks later. Here is when each state took its first legal bet: States With Legal Online Sports Betting These 31 states and Washington, DC, allow online sports betting. Each listing covers the launch date, the state regulator, the minimum age, college betting rules and which of our featured sportsbooks are available. Is Sports Betting Legal in Arizona? Arizona launched online and retail betting on the same day in September 2021, timed to the start of the NFL season. It is one of the largest markets in the West, and all six of our featured sportsbooks operate there. Is Sports Betting Legal in Arkansas? Arkansas opened casino sportsbooks in 2019 and added mobile betting in 2022, with the state's casinos running the apps. FanDuel entered in March 2026 as a partner of a casino licensee, which must keep at least 51% of the revenue. Is Sports Betting Legal in Colorado? Colorado voters approved sports betting through Proposition DD in 2019, and online and retail books opened in May 2020. It has one of the deepest app markets in the country. Is Sports Betting Legal in Connecticut? Connecticut runs a three-operator market built on agreements with the Mashantucket Pequot and Mohegan tribes and the Connecticut Lottery. Only three operators are licensed online, including FanDuel and Fanatics. Is Sports Betting Legal in Delaware? Delaware took the first legal single-game sports bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018. Online betting runs through a single lottery-contracted platform, so none of our featured sportsbooks operate there. Is Sports Betting Legal in Florida? Florida's market is controlled by the Seminole Tribe under a 2021 gaming compact, which makes Hard Rock Bet the only legal online sportsbook in the state. After a federal court fight over the compact paused the 2021 launch, Hard Rock Bet relaunched statewide in late 2023. Is Sports Betting Legal in Illinois? Illinois is one of the largest markets in the country by handle. Since July 2025 operators have paid a per-wager tax on top of a graduated revenue tax, and Chicago began taxing sportsbook revenue in January 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in Indiana? Indiana launched mobile betting in October 2019, one of the first states in the Midwest to do so. In September 2026 the Indiana Gaming Commission declined an NCAA request to ban college player props, leaving the question to lawmakers. Is Sports Betting Legal in Iowa? Iowa launched online and retail betting together in August 2019. In-person registration was required at first, but that rule ended in January 2021. Is Sports Betting Legal in Kansas? Kansas launched online betting in September 2022, with the Kansas Lottery as the operator of record. Current sportsbook contracts run through August 2027, and a 2025 budget provision barred the lottery from negotiating new ones, so the market's long-term structure is an open question. Is Sports Betting Legal in Kentucky? Kentucky launched in September 2023 with an 18 and older minimum age. In April 2026 lawmakers overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto of HB 904, which raised the betting age to 21 effective July 15, 2026, and banned under-style player props on athletes at Kentucky colleges. Is Sports Betting Legal in Louisiana? Louisiana legalized sports betting by parish-level vote in 2020, and online betting works only in the 55 of 64 parishes that approved it. The state raised its online tax rate to 21.5% in August 2025. Is Sports Betting Legal in Maine? Online betting in Maine is reserved for the state's Wabanaki Nations, which partner with national operators. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there. Is Sports Betting Legal in Maryland? Maryland voters approved sports betting in 2020, and mobile apps launched just before Thanksgiving 2022. The state raised its online tax rate from 15% to 20% in 2025. Is Sports Betting Legal in Massachusetts? Massachusetts launched mobile betting in March 2023, just ahead of March Madness. Lawmakers have debated stricter rules, including limits on props and live betting, though none had become law as of October 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in Michigan? Michigan launched online sports betting and online casino games on the same day in January 2021. bet365 became the latest major sportsbook to enter the state in April 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in Missouri? Missouri voters approved Amendment 2 in November 2024, and online and retail betting launched together on December 1, 2025. It is the newest legal market in the country. For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Missouri sports betting guide. Is Sports Betting Legal in Nevada? Nevada was the only state with full-scale legal sports betting before 2018, thanks to an exemption in federal law. Mobile apps are run by Nevada casino companies, and national brands such as FanDuel do not operate there. Is Sports Betting Legal in New Hampshire? New Hampshire runs a single-operator market through the state lottery, which keeps about half of the revenue, and none of our featured sportsbooks operate there. It is one of the few states where adults 18 and older can bet. Is Sports Betting Legal in New Jersey? New Jersey brought the case that ended the federal ban, Murphy v. NCAA, and opened its first sportsbooks in June 2018. The state raised its online sports betting tax rate to 19.75% in 2025. Is Sports Betting Legal in New York? New York is the largest legal betting market in the country by handle, with mobile apps live since January 2022. Operators pay a 51% tax on online revenue, one of the highest rates in the country. For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our New York sports betting guide. Is Sports Betting Legal in North Carolina? North Carolina launched mobile betting in March 2024, days before the ACC Tournament and March Madness. The state's July 2026 budget raised the online tax rate from 18% to 23%. For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our North Carolina sports betting guide. Is Sports Betting Legal in Ohio? Ohio launched online and retail betting together on January 1, 2023, during college football bowl season. A 2026 bill (HB 971) would sharply restrict online betting, but it had not advanced as of October 2026. For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Ohio sports betting guide. Is Sports Betting Legal in Oregon? The Oregon Lottery runs the state's online market through a single-operator partnership, and no college betting is offered on the app. Tribal casinos offer in-person betting. Is Sports Betting Legal in Pennsylvania? Pennsylvania legalized sports betting in 2017, before the federal ban was struck down, and launched online in May 2019. Its 36% tax rate on sportsbook revenue is among the highest in the country. For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Pennsylvania sports betting guide. Is Sports Betting Legal in Rhode Island? The Rhode Island Lottery runs the state's only sportsbook, available in person and through a single statewide app. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there. Is Sports Betting Legal in Tennessee? Tennessee was the first state to launch online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks. It taxes operators on the total amount wagered rather than revenue, which is unique among legal states. Is Sports Betting Legal in Vermont? Vermont launched online-only betting in January 2024 with three operators, including FanDuel and Fanatics. Is Sports Betting Legal in Virginia? Virginia launched mobile betting in January 2021, and casino sportsbooks followed in 2022. A 2026 law (HB 515) banned credit card deposits for sports betting starting July 1, 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in Washington DC? The District launched the lottery-run GambetDC app in 2020 and replaced it with FanDuel in 2024. A 2024 law change let private sportsbooks operate citywide, and bet365 became the latest to enter in September 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in West Virginia? West Virginia legalized sports betting before the Supreme Court ruling and opened its first sportsbook in August 2018. bet365 launched in the state in August 2026. Is Sports Betting Legal in Wyoming? Wyoming offers online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks, and adults 18 and older can bet. The state places no cap on the number of sportsbook licenses. States With Retail-Only Sports Betting These eight states allow sports betting only in person, usually at commercial or tribal casinos. Some offer apps, but they work only on casino property. Is Sports Betting Legal in Mississippi? Mississippi opened casino sportsbooks in August 2018, and apps such as BetMGM work only on casino property. A bill to allow statewide mobile betting passed the House for a third straight year in 2026 but died in the Senate. Is Sports Betting Legal in Montana? Montana's betting runs through the state lottery's Sports Bet Montana, available at licensed bars and taverns. The lottery app works only on those premises, so there is no statewide mobile betting. Is Sports Betting Legal in Nebraska? Nebraska allows sports betting at its licensed racetrack casinos. Voters decide don November 3, 2026, whether to legalize online sports betting through a constitutional amendment (Initiative Measure 440) and a companion statute. At the time of writing, it looks as if the vote will reject online sports betting. Is Sports Betting Legal in New Mexico? New Mexico's tribal casinos began taking bets in October 2018 under existing gaming compacts, without new state legislation. Online betting is not available. Is Sports Betting Legal in North Dakota? Sports betting in North Dakota is limited to a few tribal casinos. A 2025 proposal to put the question to voters failed, and the legislature does not meet again until 2027. Is Sports Betting Legal in South Dakota? South Dakota voters approved betting in Deadwood casinos in 2020, and bets can be placed only in person or on casino property. A 2026 plan to put statewide mobile betting on the ballot died in a House committee. Is Sports Betting Legal in Washington? Washington's tribal casinos offer sportsbooks and apps that work only on casino grounds. A 2026 law (SB 6137) began allowing bets on in-state college games while banning props on athletes at Washington schools. Is Sports Betting Legal in Wisconsin? Wisconsin legalized online betting through its tribes in April 2026, but apps have not launched because each tribal compact needs federal approval. A lawsuit filed in August 2026 challenges the law under the state constitution. States Where Sports Betting Is Not Legal Sports betting is not legal in 11 states. Here is where each one stands. Is Sports Betting Legal in Alabama? Alabama has no lottery or commercial casinos. A 2026 constitutional amendment covering a lottery, casinos and mobile betting died in committee, the third straight year a gambling bill failed. Is Sports Betting Legal in Alaska? Alaska has no legal sports betting. A mobile betting bill (HB 145) remains in committee and has never received a vote. Is Sports Betting Legal in California? California voters rejected two sports betting measures in 2022, and no measure is on the 2026 ballot. Most observers point to 2028 as the next realistic attempt, which would likely need the support of the state's tribes. Is Sports Betting Legal in Georgia? A constitutional amendment fell short of the two-thirds House vote it needed in March 2026, and the companion framework bill never reached a floor vote. Georgia's next chance comes in the 2027 session. Is Sports Betting Legal in Hawaii? Hawaii and Utah are the only states that ban all forms of gambling. Several 2026 bills stalled, and a state tourism and gaming working group is expected to report in late 2026 or early 2027. Is Sports Betting Legal in Idaho? Idaho's constitution limits gambling, and lawmakers have not seriously considered sports betting. Is Sports Betting Legal in Minnesota? Minnesota has debated sports betting for years. A tribal-run mobile betting bill failed again in 2026 amid a long-running dispute between tribes and racetracks. Is Sports Betting Legal in Oklahoma? A bill to allow tribal retail and mobile betting failed in the state Senate in April 2026. Supporters plan to try again in 2027, when a new governor takes office. Is Sports Betting Legal in South Carolina? A bill to create a state sports wagering commission received a hearing in February 2026 but did not advance. Is Sports Betting Legal in Texas? Legalization requires a constitutional amendment approved by two-thirds of both chambers and then by voters. The legislature next meets in January 2027, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick remains opposed. Is Sports Betting Legal in Utah? Utah's constitution bans all forms of gambling, and there is no effort to change it. Which States Could Legalize Sports Betting Next? Several states have active legalization efforts heading into 2027. These are the ones to watch. Legal Sportsbooks by State Not every sportsbook operates in every legal state. Here is where each of our featured sportsbooks is live online as of November 2026. Florida is the only state where Hard Rock Bet is the sole legal online option. Delaware, Rhode Island and Nevada run their own state or casino-based platforms. Prediction Markets vs Legal Sports Betting Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket let users trade contracts on the outcome of sporting events. They operate under federal oversight from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) rather than state gaming licenses, which is why they are available in some states where sportsbooks are not legal, including California and Texas. Many states argue these contracts are sports betting and should require a state license. Federal appeals courts have split. The Third Circuit sided with Kalshi against New Jersey in April 2026, while the Ninth Circuit (Nevada, August 2026) and the Sixth Circuit (Ohio and Tennessee, September 2026) ruled that states can regulate sports event contracts. New Jersey has asked the US Supreme Court to take up the issue. Prediction markets are not the same as a licensed sportsbook. They are not overseen by state gaming regulators, and state responsible gambling protections may not apply. FanDuel also runs a separate product, FanDuel Predicts, which offers sports contracts only in states where FanDuel Sportsbook is not available. Is Offshore Sports Betting Legal? Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed or regulated by any US state. They often advertise to bettors in states without legal betting, but they offer no protection if a site refuses to pay, freezes an account or shuts down. Licensed sportsbooks must verify your identity and location, keep player funds separate, follow state advertising rules and offer responsible gambling tools. If a sportsbook is not listed by your state regulator, it is not legal where you live. Sports Betting Rules Every Bettor Should Know What Is the Legal Age to Bet on Sports? The minimum age is 21 in most states. Adults 18 and older can bet in New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC, though some sportsbooks in DC, including BetMGM, set their own minimum of 21. In Washington, the age depends on the tribal casino. Kentucky raised its minimum age from 18 to 21 on July 15, 2026. Do You Have to Live in a State to Bet There? No. You only need to be physically located inside a legal state when you place a bet. Sportsbook apps use geolocation to confirm your location, so visitors can sign up and bet while they are in the state. Can You Bet From a State Where Sports Betting Is Not Legal? No. If you travel into a state without legal betting, your app will block wagers until you return to a legal state. You can usually still log in, view your account and withdraw funds. What Are College Betting Restrictions? Many states limit college betting. The most common rules ban bets on in-state college teams, ban player props on college athletes, or both. Restrictions are listed in each state's section above. How to Start Betting Legally Responsible Gambling Sports betting should always be entertainment. If gambling stops being fun, these free and confidential resources can help. Every legal sportsbook also offers deposit limits, time limits and self-exclusion tools, and most state regulators run their own self-exclusion programs. Where Is Sports Betting Legal FAQs How many states have legal sports betting? Sports betting is legal in 39 states and Washington, DC, as of November 2026. Online betting is live in 31 of those states plus DC, while eight states allow only in-person betting. Is online sports betting legal in my state? Online betting is live in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming and Washington DC. Which states do not allow sports betting? Sports betting is not legal in Alabama, Alaska, California, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Minnesota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas and Utah. When did sports betting become legal in the US? The Supreme Court struck down the federal ban (PASPA) on May 14, 2018. Delaware took the first legal bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018, and New Jersey followed days later. What is the legal age to bet on sports? The minimum age is 21 in most states. New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC allow betting at 18, though some sportsbooks set a higher minimum. Can I bet on sports if I am visiting a legal state? Yes. You do not need to be a resident. You only need to be physically located in a legal state when you place your bet. Which state will legalize sports betting next? Nebraska voters decided on online betting on November 3, 2026, and Wisconsin has legalized online betting but not yet launched. Texas, Georgia and Oklahoma are the largest states expected to revisit legalization in 2027. Are prediction markets like Kalshi legal sports betting? Prediction markets operate under federal CFTC oversight rather than state gaming licenses, so they are not licensed sportsbooks. Several states are challenging them in court, and their legal status in some states remains unsettled.

Point Spread In baseball, you can only score 1-4 runs at a time. In basketball, you get either 1, 2, or 3 points at a time. Football is built on 3s and 6s (with 7 being a key number due to extra points). A point spread means that one team needs to win or lose by adding or subtracting the point spread from their final score vs. their opponent’s final score. Moneyline A simpler bet is the moneyline. If it is a negative number, they are the favorite. If there is a plus next to their number, it means the team is an underdog to win the game. You don’t need to worry about the final score, just whoever wins. Totals (Over/Under) Totals are offered on the combined points scored between the two teams. Often you’ll see rain or snow impacting the total for games, and it will drop significantly. Conversely, ideal weather might help make the total increase. Team totals only focus on the individual team’s score. Player Props Player props are bets that focus on one specific player. You can pick almost any offensive player and bet on what they specifically will contribute to the game. You can bet on passing yardage, rushing, or receiving yardage. Another common bet is on whether a player will score a touchdown or not. For a wager like that, know that if you take a quarterback, they need to score; it does not count if they throw the ball to a teammate. Those are a different type of prop bet: touchdown passes. Same Game Parlays Same Game Parlays take multiple things that you think will happen in one game and combine them for one bet. If one leg of the parlay is incorrect, the Same Game Parlay is graded as a loss. These don’t often pay as high because everything is correlated. Teasers Teasers are somewhat like parlays, but you can change the spreads or totals when using them. You take two or more teams/numbers and subtract or add to the total. Most common are six- and seven-point teasers. This can change a big favorite into just needing to win by a smaller score, or give an underdog even more points for the game. NFL Futures and Season-Long Bets Future bets are very common in the NFL because it has one of the shorter seasons in professional sports. Wagering before the season still ties up funds, and most won’t be cashed out until the season is over. Some sportsbooks pay a winning wager as soon as it hits, for example if a team wins 10 games on over 9.5 wins, the wager is paid immediately. It is common for bettors to place futures on individuals or teams, and while many are placed before the season, markets are offered all year. articles.title: A 50ft coconut tree crushed a British woman while she was sunbathing at a Sri Lankan resort, leaving her with 10 operations; she is now suing her former lawyers for £4.5 million over a wrong email
articles.summary: A British woman who suffered severe injuries after a 50ft coconut palm tree fell on her while she was sunbathing at a Sri Lankan hotel is suing her former
articles.body: A British woman who suffered severe injuries after a 50ft coconut palm tree fell on her while she was sunbathing at a Sri Lankan hotel is suing her former solicitors for £4.5 million. Claire Saywell, who required around 10 operations following the 2017 accident, claims Slater and Gordon UK Ltd cost her the chance to secure compensation from travel company TUI by sending legal documents to the wrong email address. The firm has admitted breaching its professional duty but disputes whether her original claim would have succeeded, with the case now being considered at London's High Court.How a falling coconut tree left Claire Saywell with severe leg injuriesAccording to the Sun, the incident happened in 2017 when Claire Saywell was holidaying with her husband at the four-star Club Hotel Dolphin in Waikkal, a town in western Sri Lanka. She was relaxing on a sun lounger near the hotel's pool when a large coconut palm tree suddenly fell on her legs. The impact left her legs severely damaged, with her knees reportedly bent backwards into a "V-shape". The accident resulted in serious injuries that required extensive medical treatment.Following the incident, Saywell underwent emergency surgery in Colombo, Sri Lanka's capital, before being flown back to her home in Sittingbourne, Kent. She subsequently required approximately 10 operations on her legs and has continued to experience significant pain and mobility problems. During a preliminary hearing at the High Court, her barrister, Howard Elgot, explained that she had suffered "serious pain and continuing disabilities in relation to her legs". He also told the court that she had been forced to give up her job as a well-paid peripatetic insurance executive and was now unemployed. According to the submissions, her injuries mean she requires single-storey accommodation.Wrong email address caused TUI compensation claim to collapseAfter the accident, Saywell instructed law firm Slater and Gordon UK Ltd to pursue a personal injury claim against TUI, the travel company through which she had booked her holiday. However, the original case did not proceed because her solicitors failed to serve the claim form within the required time. The central issue was that the legal documents initiating the proceedings were sent to the wrong email address for TUI's solicitors, meaning the claim was not validly served.At the preliminary hearing, Howard Elgot described the proceedings as a professional negligence claim against Saywell's former solicitors. He told Master John Dagnall: "Breach of duty by the defendant is admitted. They failed to validly serve Mrs Saywell's claim form in her personal injury claim against Tui UK Ltd and her claim was struck out." The firm has therefore acknowledged that it failed to meet its professional obligations in handling the original proceedings. However, admitting the breach does not automatically establish that Saywell is entitled to the compensation she is seeking, as the firm continues to dispute whether the original claim would have succeeded.Evidence of tree rot emerges in Sri Lankan hotel accident caseThe circumstances surrounding the falling tree have also become an important part of the legal dispute. According to the submissions presented by Elgot, the pool area at Club Hotel Dolphin was surrounded by several well-established coconut trees. Saywell's legal team maintains that the palm fell without warning, causing severe and permanent injuries. The defendant's allegations, as outlined in a written statement by the barrister, included the possibility that the tree had fallen because of strong winds.However, a tree expert appointed by the court reportedly identified evidence of damage at the base of the palm. The expert found that "a spike and concrete had been driven into the base of the tree". The assessment concluded that this had caused "rot and damage to the trunk". Elgot explained that coconut trees would not ordinarily fall during high winds unless they were already rotten. Saywell's legal team argues that this evidence could have supported her original claim against TUI had the proceedings been allowed to continue. Her barrister told the court that she believed she had "more than a negligible chance of success" if the evidence had been presented in the original case.Slater and Gordon disputes £4.5 million compensation claim over TUI lawsuitSlater and Gordon UK Ltd is contesting the compensation claim, arguing that Saywell's original case against TUI was unlikely to succeed. Representing the firm, Clare Elliot told the court that the proposed claim against the travel company "didn't exceed the 51% likelihood of success". She also challenged the amount being sought, describing the £4.5 million damages figure as "highly contested". The dispute therefore centres not only on the admitted failure to serve the original claim correctly but also on whether that failure caused Saywell to lose a realistic opportunity to obtain compensation from TUI.Master John Dagnall permitted Saywell to call the tree expert as part of the proceedings. Explaining the nature of the case, he described it as "a solicitors' negligence claim, arising from an accident arising from a falling coconut palm tree on holiday in Sri Lanka". He also confirmed that the defendants had failed to serve the claim form in time, resulting in the original claim being struck out. The judge characterised the proceedings as a "loss of a chance claim". The court also heard that both sides would attempt to resolve the dispute through alternative dispute resolution if possible. The proceedings concern whether the solicitors' admitted failure deprived Saywell of a genuine opportunity to pursue her original personal injury claim and whether she is entitled to the £4.5 million in damages she is seeking.You use AI every day. articles.title: Photos: Pope Leo visits Peru’s Amazon and Andean regions during 12-day tour
articles.summary: The pope has called for the preservation of Indigenous traditions in Peru as he wraps up a 12-day tour of Latin America.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has criss-crossed Peru on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour, making stops in the Andean highlands and the Peruvian Amazon.

Sunday marked the last full day of his trip, which has seen him visit Uruguay and Argentina already.

The pontiff spent the morning in the Andean city of Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire, delivering a speech at the Indigenous fortress of Saqsaywaman.

In his remarks, Leo praised the region’s traditional festivities and processions, which often blend Indigenous and Catholic spirituality.

“The future of these traditions lies not only in preserving what has been handed down, but also in passing it on in a living way,” he said.

Huge crowds also packed Cusco’s central Plaza de Armas to greet Leo. Though born in the United States, Leo acquired Peruvian citizenship in 2015, after living in the country for years and later becoming the bishop of Chiclayo , a major city in the north.

Leo is the first Peruvian citizen to become pope.

The visit to Cusco, a high-altitude city some 3,400 metres (more than 11,000 feet) above sea level, tested the 71-year-old pope’s stamina as he continues to recover from lung cancer surgery.

Leo, however, has shown no sign of fatigue since his 12-day, three-nation South American trip began on November 6.

In the afternoon, Leo flew to Pucallpa, a city near Peru’s eastern border, on the banks of the Ucayali River.

Pucallpa is considered a gateway to the Peruvian Amazon, and during his stay, Leo reinforced his late predecessor Pope Francis’s teachings on protecting the environment.

He also denounced the violence faced by Indigenous land defenders, who use their advocacy to confront deforestation, pollution and the threat of Indigenous expulsion.

“Many Indigenous leaders have been murdered for defending their territories,” Leo said. “The blood of these brothers cries out ⁠to God and demands justice.”

Indigenous communities have long been threatened by illegal mining, deforestation and other forms of exploitation. Mining has also led to a water crisis in Peru, with pollution leading to an increased risk of heavy metal poisoning.

Leo is expected to return to Rome on Monday.

articles.body: Before Dunkin' became a household name for coffee and donuts, its founder tried to build a fast-food business around a TV puppet. William Rosenberg, who founded Dunkin' Donuts, launched Howdy Beef N' Burger in New England in 1961. At its peak, the chain had about 30 locations, some of which operated alongside Dunkin' Donuts. The retro chain was originally called Howdy Beefburger before changing to Howdy Beef N’ Burger, according to reports. RETRO PIZZA HUT DRAWS CUSTOMERS FROM HOURS AWAY AS 1980S NOSTALGIA SENDS SALES SOARING The regional chain took its name and mascot from Howdy Doody, the beloved cowboy marionette who starred in a children's show that aired on NBC from 1947 to 1960, according to food website Chowhound. The show featured the puppet and human characters in skits and songs before a studio audience of children known as the "peanut gallery." Aside from burgers and fries, the chain also served a signature Big "B" burger. It also served roast beef sandwiches, fried chicken, shakes and New England seafood dishes such as clam strips, chowder and lobster rolls, according to the food history blog Burger Beast. FAST-FOOD CHAIN THAT ONCE LIT UP AMERICAN ROADS STILL MISSED DECADES LATER Promotions leaned into the chain’s family appeal. A Boston Globe ad, cited by The Takeout, promised diners could "feed the family on just pocket change." The chain also offered burger deals and prizes, giveaways and buttons for children, according to reports. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER But Howdy's reportedly faced competition from McDonald’s, plus Rosenberg’s company had other ventures to manage, including seafood, pancakes and deli businesses. When his son Robert became company president in 1963, he began narrowing the company’s focus to Dunkin’ Donuts, Chowhound reported. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS While Dunkin' continued to grow, Howdy's faded, with some locations sold off to other restaurant chains. A Quincy, Massachusetts, restaurant became a Wendy’s in 1979, according to Burger Beast. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ By the 1980s, the chain had largely disappeared, according to Chowhound. Today, the New England burger chain survives in vintage ads, nostalgic memorabilia and diners' memories. Howdy Doody wasn’t the only fictional character to inspire a restaurant, though. articles.title: Iran vows ‘we will find you’ to 2 US Navy officers the day warship returns from Middle East
articles.summary: Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a "We will find you" threat targeting two USS Spruance officers as the destroyer returned to San Diego.
articles.body: Iran’s embassy in South Africa threatened two U.S. Navy officers with a "We will find you" message online as their warship returned to San Diego on Friday after a historic 357-day deployment that included combat against Iranian forces. The warning, posted on X on Nov. 13 alongside images identifying the USS Spruance’s commanding officer and executive officer, prompted a regional expert to warn that Iran’s public targeting of American service members should set off alarm bells in Washington. The embassy identified Cmdr. Leigh R. Tate, commanding officer of the Spruance, and Lt. Cmdr. Jeffrey E. York, the ship’s executive officer. IRAN MINES US TROOPS' SOCIAL MEDIA AS MILITARY CONSIDERS SEIZING CELLPHONES "We will find you," the embassy wrote on X. The embassy had previously singled out the officers in a March 28 post accusing them of ordering Tomahawk missile launches that killed 168 children at an elementary school in Minab, Iran. "Remember these two criminals," the earlier post began. "Don’t they have children of their own?" the embassy asked at the time. Behnam Ben Taleblu, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, warned that the rhetoric coming out of Tehran should be taken seriously given Iran’s history of plotting attacks against American officials. "This should be setting off alarm bells in Washington, in the White House, the Pentagon, and even within CENTCOM," Taleblu told Fox News Digital. "The Islamic Republic has literally identified personnel that they allege are involved in strikes against the regime, and they’re talking about retribution." "If indeed there is any plot to go after these individuals, it is critical they’re detected, they are disrupted, they are defeated," Taleblu warned. IRAN-BACKED TERROR SUSPECTS PLOTTED ATTACK ON US TROOPS USING VANS PACKED WITH FUEL, DOJ SAYS The threat from Iran came a day after President Donald Trump warned Tehran against assassinating senior American officials. During a Nov. 12 interview with radio host Hugh Hewitt, Trump was asked what would happen if Iran killed a senior U.S. official. "They will not exist very long, any longer," Trump responded. His warning also followed reports that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had relocated from his Washington-area residence to a military base amid Iranian threats against his life. Bessent confirmed the move during a Friday interview on CNBC, saying he was following Secret Service instructions. "Why am I going to be afraid when the brave military personnel in the Gulf, President Trump, constantly receive death threats?" Bessent asked. Bessent described Iran as behaving "like a dangerous cornered animal" and insisted the threats would not derail the administration’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran. TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and senior White House official Stephen Miller have also reportedly moved into military or other protected housing amid security concerns. In another post on X, the Iranian embassy in South Africa went on to mock senior administration officials over their security arrangements. "Rubio, Bessent, Hegseth, and other U.S. officials live in constant fear, haunted by the crimes committed, and now confined to military bunkers for their own protection," the embassy wrote, suggesting they should occasionally appear in public. The threats come as federal authorities have announced developments in alleged Iranian-backed plots targeting Americans. On Nov. 10, the FBI added Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps operative Shahram Poursafi to its Most Wanted Terrorists list over an alleged assassination plot targeting former senior U.S. officials, including former national security adviser John Bolton. That same day, the Justice Department announced terrorism charges against three men accused of involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States, including an alleged plot targeting a British air base housing American forces. The developments followed an Oct. 23 U.S. intelligence warning that Iranian efforts to target American personnel abroad had substantially increased, with some plots reaching advanced stages. TRUMP'S TOP OFFICIALS RETREAT BEHIND MILITARY GATES AS EX-FBI DEPUTY POINTS TO WHAT'S FUELING THREATS The embassy’s warning coincided with the Spruance’s return to Naval Base San Diego on Nov. 13, ending the longest deployment by a U.S. Navy destroyer since World War II. The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer departed San Diego on Nov. 21, 2025, alongside the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group. Its deployment was extended as American forces conducted Operation Epic Fury against Iran. The Spruance traveled more than 88,000 nautical miles during the deployment and launched dozens of Tomahawk land-attack cruise missiles against Iranian military targets between February and August 2026, according to a statement released by the Navy. The ship also destroyed 12 unmanned aerial vehicles and four anti-ship cruise missiles while operating under persistent threats from Iranian drones and missiles. "Spruance, in particular, as the alternate air defense commander was, I would say, instrumental in defending the carrier, defending the force from those inbound threats," Tate said Friday in the statement. CENTCOM COMMANDER TOUTS USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN MENTAL HEALTH RECORD AFTER MORE THAN 260 DAYS WITHOUT PORT CALL The destroyer also participated in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. In April, it intercepted the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska after the ship failed to comply with repeated American warnings. U.S. Central Command said at the time that the Spruance ordered the vessel’s engine room evacuated before firing rounds that disabled the ship. Tate called commanding the ship during the extended deployment an "honor of a lifetime." "Spruance sailors made a difference," Tate also said in a statement Friday. "They represented their families, their ship and the United States Navy with distinction." Meanwhile, Iranian officials have also been threatening U.S. military installations overseas. On Nov. 11, Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran could strike American bases in Europe if the United States resumed attacks on Iran. ANOTHER TRUMP HEAVYWEIGHT REVEALED TO BE LIVING ON MILITARY BASE AS CABINET ROSTER GROWS "If the Americans make a mistake and attack us, we will not limit ourselves to nearby bases," Rezaei told Al Mayadeen. Taleblu described the embassy’s latest statements as part of an escalating pattern of threats against American personnel. "This is an escalation of the course that we’ve been on," he said, pointing to threatening rhetoric from Iranian diplomatic accounts and hard-line commentators during and after the war. "So this is basically incitement and invective from the world’s foremost state sponsor of terrorism, one which unfortunately has a track record of carrying these things out, even with a delay." He pointed to threats against U.S. military personnel following the accidental American shootdown of an Iranian civilian airliner in 1988. articles.body: Powersheds, the modular garden shed company co-founded in 2019 by Jack Sutcliffe and Simon Hobson, shows how two former shed factory employees built a leading United Kingdom manufacturer from early eBay sales. The pair sold just 14 sheds in their first month, making, painting and dispatching every one themselves. Today the business is described as the country’s most awarded shed manufacturer, with annual turnover above £15 million, a workforce of 80 and expansion into Europe. Its rise offers small business owners in any industry clear, practical lessons on modular design, online retail, sound financial systems and well-timed outside investment.Difficulty judging shed quality online inspired a modular design customers could customiseAccording to UHY Hacker Young, the idea for Powersheds took shape in 2019, when the founders noticed that shoppers struggled to judge shed quality online, particularly when buying online. They envisioned a modular garden building that paired modern design with the simplicity of a traditional shed, letting customers choose where the doors and windows go. Pieces could be sent out much like a parcel over the pallet network. Both men were working at a shed manufacturing facility in Leeds when they met a partner from the firm’s Leeds office. They knew their idea was unique but were unsure where to start. After extensive discussion and planning, they took a leap of faith and left their jobs.Turnover rose from £1 million to £5 million and then £14 million within three years of the ideaTurnover reached £1 million after one year in business and £5 million within two. By the year ending 28 February 2022 it had climbed to £14 million, and it has since passed £15 million. Chief executive Jack Sutcliffe, via UHY Hacker Young in a separate interview, said that launching just months before a global pandemic made the early days a real challenge.Moving from basic spreadsheets to comprehensive software gave fast growth a firm footingWith the business growing so quickly, the advisers first helped the founders raise finance for their early expansion. They then helped replace rudimentary spreadsheets with software covering stock control and order processing. In the early days, partner Gordon Gruppetta ran bookkeeping training sessions for Sutcliffe so the company could build solid financial foundations. The team also trained staff on the new systems and seconded support teams so that management reporting stayed seamless.BSW Group, its main timber supplier, bought half of the business less than four years after launchRapid retail success left the business cash rich, so partners at the Leeds office held strategic sessions with the founders on what prosperity meant to them. Further investment emerged as the next step, and discussions with venture capital firms produced compelling offers before a deal was struck for an undisclosed sum. Sutcliffe remained chief executive, with Hobson as a director. articles.title: US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
articles.summary: Scott Bessent gives Nvidia’s board 10 days to show the company’s compliance with US export controls.
articles.body:
United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for an outsider to take the helm at Nvidia, the California-based technology giant that has faced scandal over its former chief executive, Jensen Huang .

Speaking on Fox News’s Sunday Morning Futures programme, Bessent said the company should look beyond its own ranks for Huang’s successor.

“This makes me think that, as the board conducts a search for a new leader, that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent told Fox News. “Just [with] what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shake-up.”

Bessent’s comments come three days after Huang stepped down on Thursday, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman US officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence .

Nvidia plays a leading role in producing chips and other computing components for artificial intelligence (AI).

As a result, the company has been at the centre of a technology race between the US and China, with the two superpowers competing for dominance in the growing AI sector.

Huang was long a key figure at Nvidia, as one of the company’s cofounders. Since 2025, he has also cultivated a close relationship with the second administration of US President Donald Trump.

In August 2025, for instance, Huang successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen restrictions on the sale of H20 microchips to China, in exchange for the US government taking 15 percent of the sales.

But in late October, The New York Times revealed Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s clients.

The report cited unnamed US intelligence agents who believed Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to help the country’s firms navigate US chip restrictions.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Beijing has denied the allegations, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Alice Huang has not publicly commented on the claims. She reportedly left Megaspeed in 2025.

For his part, Jensen Huang had long maintained that wider access to US technology would help Washington preserve its edge in the global AI race.

Bessent, however, questioned whether Nvidia had turned a blind eye to potentially illicit chip sales to bolster its financial results.

In Sunday’s television appearance, Bessent suggested a 10-day deadline for the company to show its compliance with US export controls.

“I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel,” Bessent said.

“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?”

The controversy has encouraged a bipartisan push in Congress to tighten controls on US chip exports to China.

Lawmakers, including Republican Senator Jim Banks and Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, have sought to use the annual end-of-year defence bill to close loopholes that Chinese companies can exploit to obtain advanced US-designed semiconductors.

But Bessent questioned the need for new laws, telling Fox News host Larry Kudlow that Washington’s existing export controls were sufficient but needed better enforcement.

“I don’t think we need the legislation,” he said. “We have all the rules we need; we just need them enforced.”

Since Huang’s departure, rumours have swirled about who might replace him at Nvidia’s helm.

The company’s board has floated Rene Haas, the chief executive of the semiconductor firm Arm Holdings, as a possible successor to Huang, according to the Financial Times.

Haas is no stranger to Nvidia, having spent several years at the company before joining the British chip designer.

Trump, meanwhile, has named former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as a potential candidate .

In a post on Truth Social on Thursday, Trump praised Huang’s work at Nvidia and said Cook was an ideal candidate to replace him.

“A Legend replaces a Legend,” Trump wrote.

But the Financial Times has suggested Huang may seek to return to his top-level post. In a report on Sunday, the publication said unnamed allies of his are rallying Silicon Valley executives to support his return to the company.

“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” one source told the Financial Times.

Currently, chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading Nvidia on an interim basis.

articles.title: Rivals mansion where Danny Dyer's character lives drops asking price
articles.summary: The house was put up for sale with an £8m price tag in May before estate agents cut it to £6.5m.
articles.body:
A mansion that is home to Danny Dyer's character on Disney+ series Rivals has dropped in price by £1.5m after failing to woo buyers.

The house, called Bella Vista on the show, is in Lisvane, Cardiff, and was put up for sale with an £8m price tag in May before estate agents reduced it to £6.5m this month.

Based on one of Dame Jilly Cooper's so-called "bonkbuster" novels, Rivals features an all-star cast including David Tennant and Emily Atack, and more episodes of season two were released on Wednesday.

The site up for sale is 24 acres, and includes a tennis court, wine cellar and a gym - and is one of Wales' most expensive homes.

Built in 1999 and called Foxfield, it was previously occupied by businessman Peter Thomas.

Estate agent Jemma Friday said: "Properties of this scale and calibre are incredibly rare in Cardiff, and this new guide price presents an exciting opportunity for prospective buyers."

The property is listed as having seven en-suite bedrooms, a valet car garage and a large drawing room, according to the Fine and Country website.

Rivals is the second of Cooper's hugely successful Rutshire Chronicles, a series of books that chronicle the lives of English upper and upper-middle classes in a fictional area of the Cotswolds, originally published in 1988.

Set against the backdrop of 1980s excess and large country estates, the series tells the story of the rivalry between the aristocratic Rupert Campbell-Black and TV executive Lord Tony Baddingham.

Dame Jilly Cooper died in 2025 aged 88 , but made headlines earlier this year after asking the executive producers of the show to stop making her macho men cry on screen .

articles.title: Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine
articles.summary: He has been showing support for injured veterans in Ukraine and praising the country's resilience.
articles.body:
The Duke of Sussex has received an enthusiastic welcome in a surprise visit to Ukraine to support injured war veterans, meeting Ukrainian competitors taking part in his Invictus Games.

There were emotional scenes as he was applauded by injured service men and women in Lviv, where he told his audience: "You're going to win the war."

Prince Harry spent two days at events for veterans, with a press blackout for security reasons until he had left Ukraine, as the country continues to face missile attacks from Russia.

Ukraine has more than 150,000 injured war veterans and the prince visited projects supporting their treatment and rehabilitation.

"Ukraine now is experiencing elements of war that no other country has experienced before," he said - with technology advancing in areas such as drone warfare, but also in protecting cities and providing treatment.

A mobile phone app is where Ukrainians look for air raid warnings, telling them the direction, timing and type of any incoming missiles.

At the Superhumans Center near Lviv, Harry was shown how growing numbers of injured veterans receive groundbreaking treatment.

International experts used to come to help Ukraine, he said, but "now that has flipped," with Ukraine having the greater expertise with trauma injuries to share with others.

That included an innovation for Mykhailo Damaskin, a Ukrainian air assault forces veteran, who was so seriously injured in fighting in Kherson he was never expected to walk again.

In an experimental treatment he had a spinal cord stimulator implanted in his back, which allows him to walk, but has to be re-charged every 12 hours. He cannot feel his feet and controls his steps using his eyes.

He needs to be plugged in and charged up to be able to move - and jokes that he is "like a demo model of a Tesla".

"My goal is to go to the Invictus Games. I promised my father before he was killed that I'd be part of the team to represent Ukraine internationally.

"I'll prove to every guy with spinal cord injuries that life goes on after injury," said Mykhailo.

At the Superhumans Center Prince Harry sat at the bedside of Konstiantyn Vlasenko, who was airlifted from the front line by a drone last month in a rescue that was a first of its kind.

He had been alone for more than 200 days and had stayed at his position, despite losing both his feet.

In a moving encounter, Prince Harry told him he represented the spirit of resilience of Ukraine.

And he described the injured veterans as "role models", promising his audience: "The rest of the world will continue to support you."

Along with all the determination, it was an inescapably poignant sight too, with so many families and children at the medical facility visiting the growing numbers of badly injured war casualties.

At a noisy sports centre, Prince Harry arrived to watch a wheelchair rugby match taking place, with some thunderous collisions between the players.

He was welcomed by the competitors in what he has called his Invictus "family" and soon the visit turned into something approaching a group hug, with Harry disappearing into a sea of selfies and handshakes.

He was presented with a T-shirt remembering prisoners of war held by Russian forces.

And he later had a chance to play one of the events at the Invictus Games, a tennis-style competition called pickleball.

Watching was Ivan Voinov, who has lost a leg and suffered head injuries, but who is using sport to help his rehabilitation - including learning to dance again.

He said that dancing was his way to be together with his wife again, which meant so much to his recovery and recovering his identity.

At an Invictus awards ceremony during the visit, Prince Harry was greeted with choruses of "Harry, Harry, Harry", getting a rock star welcome.

"Every single time I come back to Ukraine, I feel welcome, I feel warmth, I feel encouragement," he said, having returned for a fourth trip here during wartime.

He promised that "when the war is over and when Ukraine wins, we will be ready to support you in holding an Invictus Games".

There have been 400 wounded service men and women in Ukraine taking part in trials for next year's games, being hosted in Birmingham.

The sports events are an attempt to encourage rehabilitation and to recognise the resilience of people overcoming their challenges.

Prince Harry told a gathering of new Invictus members of a "cultural shift" from people being socially awkward about seeing injured veterans to wanting to show respect.

"These people have so much to offer," he said.

"Recovery cannot wait for the war to end, The scale of need in Ukraine is huge, and wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans need the chance to rebuild their lives now," said Rob Owen, chief executive officer of the Invictus Games Foundation.

articles.title: UK will have 'voice' but no vote on EU food rules in Brexit reset
articles.summary: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
articles.body:
The UK will have a "voice in the room" but no vote on European Union food policies as part of a so-called "Brexit reset" to reduce red tape, EU relations minister Hamish Falconer has told the BBC.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham hopes to agree a deal at a summit on Friday but critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker" but not a rule maker.

Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules and said the deal could help bring down prices for shoppers.

The reset would not involve any upfront payments, Falconer added, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment.

Falconer said it was "reasonable" to consider what would happen if a future Conservative or Reform government wanted to undo the new arrangements.

"The EU is worried about that and you can see why," he said.

The BBC understands that the clause is a result of EU concerns about the possible cost of having to rebuild facilities for border food safety checks which were put in place following Brexit.

The reset means they will be dismantled.

In September, the Conservative Party said it was "raising the alarm" over the government's planned reset, saying it would leave British consumers and businesses "dangerously exposed, with no input on how regulations are made or power to reject them".

Both the Conservatives and Reform have said they would undo the planned reset if they were in power.

The prime minister has said he believes there is a "win-win" deal to be had with the EU.

Speaking at a Marks & Spencer food court in central London, Falconer said the deal would help bring down costs for firms importing food.

"This will mean less cost for supermarkets, and I hope that less cost then turns into cheaper produce on the shelves," he said.

He said currently "pages and pages" of form-filling meant some suppliers had given up exporting to the EU and some products, such as Lincolnshire sausages, meant they were almost impossible to export at all.

Some M&S trucks require over 300 pages of documents for food exports, from export health certificates, phytosanitary certificates, visits from vets and border check paperwork.

Some exports are rejected for having the wrong colour of ink on forms, or an inaccurate Latin name for cooked meats.

"The amount of paperwork you would need to do, the amount of uncertainty - you have to have it in the right pen colour, if it's not black, it might be refused," Falconer said.

"If you're selling Cox apples from Kent, they have to wait a day before they go into the European Union."

The reset could also mean "tearing up" checks that were introduced on goods flowing from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, following Brexit, he said, as well as separate "Not for EU" labelling.

Falconer said the impact of the reset deal for food would be an additional £5bn.

The whole deal to be signed on Friday is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP.

This wider agreement includes aligning emissions trading rules, and agreeing to a youth mobility scheme, as well as the reset on food trading.

Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers' Union, welcomed reduced border inspections and paperwork but said that for the NFU it was "a moment of opportunity and risk" with farmers waiting to see what carve-outs and transitional arrangements would be included.

Trade volumes in food exports to the EU had "fallen significantly - by over a third" since 2019, he said.

But the UK should take a "pragmatic" approach to implementing any new rules.

He raised pesticides and precision breeding - or gene edited crops - as areas where he hoped some compromise would be found.

UK firms are, for example, developing tomatoes engineered to contain extra vitamin D.

Historically the EU has had much stricter rules on gene-editing, but this year relaxed regulations.

Falconer said people would have to "wait and see the detail" in this area.

He said there were bound to be compromises and trade-offs in any deal but that where the UK had advantages the government wanted to make sure "those aren't lost under the deal".

Another contentious area has been crisp flavourings, with concerns raised that stricter EU rules on certain ingredients might limit the sale of some popular snack flavours in the UK.

"I want to take this opportunity to absolutely stamp down on misinformation about smoky bacon crisps," Falconer said.

Post-Brexit the UK had stayed "pretty closely aligned" to European food safety standards, he said.

Two leading snack brands had already adapted their recipes to accommodate EU rules, an example of the kind of alignment that would happen whether or not there was a reset of UK-EU relations.

"The truth is, almost every business in this country that wants to export food or drink will be aligning with EU rules because it's our biggest market.

"Lots of people, like the good people at Walkers and Frazzles have made these changes already, so I would want to reassure people, particularly smoky bacon fans, it's okay," he said.

articles.title: Brand moved from Wandsworth to category C prison HMP Littlehey, his wife confirms
articles.summary: The convicted rapist has been moved to HMP Littlehey, which houses sex offenders.
articles.body:
Russell Brand has been transferred to a category C prison, his wife Laura has confirmed, in her first public comments since his jailing.

On Monday, the comedian was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Over the weekend, Brand was transferred from category B HMP Wandsworth in London to HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire, which houses men convicted of sexual offences.

Laura Brand returned to the couple's podcast on Sunday, saying that she had spoken to her husband in prison and he "is OK and is praying". Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.

HMP Littlehey, a category C training prison, is one of the largest prisons in Europe for men convicted of sexual offences.

It held more than 1,200 prisoners as of January 2025, according to data from the Independent Monitoring Board.

Before Brand's move to the prison, a source close to the disgraced comedian said he was doing "remarkably well considering the circumstances" at HMP Wandsworth and that he had been moved from isolation to a main wing.

A member of staff at Wandsworth said there had been "much excitement" among the inmates about Brand's arrival, with some slamming on cell doors and shouting out his name. They added that there had also been some anger displayed about his crimes.

Staff at other prisons told the BBC Brand's fame, combined with the nature of his crimes, could make him a target for other inmates.

In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can seen sitting on a sofa in what looks like a conservatory. She is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.

The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know

Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

The couple had continued their YouTube podcast during Brand's trial. They often read snippets of the Bible and discussed religion.

On Sunday, Laura told their followers: "We trust his [God's] plan and everything he is doing just now, even though it's painful and obviously will take some getting used to."

During the show, Laura played an episode she said had been recorded before her husband was jailed.

It featured the couple singing to the American folk singer Woody Guthrie before praying together.

Towards the end of the podcast, Laura returned on her own to read a message from her husband, in which he said he was not guilty for the offences he had been jailed for.

He called staff at HMP Littlehey "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and he asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".

articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
articles.summary: The countries accuse Israel of preventing tents and other supplies from entering Gaza, despite the humanitarian crisis.
articles.body:
Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom have ⁠⁠⁠⁠urged Israel to allow immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza, highlighting that recent floods have “brought further suffering” for Palestinians living there.

The countries’ foreign ministers co-signed Sunday’s joint statement , the latest international warning about the dire humanitarian situation in the besieged territory.

“People in Gaza desperately need shelter and humanitarian assistance,” the statement said. “Yet 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering Gaza.”

For years, Israel has restricted entry and exports into Gaza, home to more than 2 million people.

But since the start of its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israel has placed the Palestinian territory under a full-scale blockade, limiting access to even essential supplies like food and water.

Under the Geneva Convention, denying civilians access to humanitarian aid can constitute a war crime.

“We today urge the Government of Israel to stop the delays now and allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza,” Sunday’s statement said.

Heavy rain this month swept away tens of thousands of tents in the territory, leaving many without shelter.

“This situation is entirely reversible”, Sunday’s statement said, “and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in”.

More than 1.9 million people have been displaced in Gaza, according to the United Nations, many of them suffering displacement multiple times.

As of November 1, the Global Shelter Cluster, a humanitarian organisation that coordinates with the Red Cross and the UN, estimated that Gaza residents need at least 1.7 million mattresses and 121,000 tents to face this season’s cold, rainy weather.

During Israel’s genocidal war, entire neighbourhoods and cities were levelled. Some of the structures that remain are unstable.

In September, at least 20 people were killed when a building they were sheltering in collapsed.

Shelter is only one factor in the ongoing humanitarian crisis, though.

Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have been plunged into poverty since Israel began its genocidal war. The price of basic goods has soared as incomes have shrunk due to the war and Israel’s tightened siege.

Sunday’s statement follows a similar appeal from the UN’s Humanitarian Country Team of the Occupied Palestinian Territory on Friday.

“The devastating impact of the latest rainstorm in Gaza was preventable,” the team wrote.

“Children and adults were killed, critical services suspended, and thousands of family shelters flooded, swept away, or torn apart – not by the storm alone, but by policy decisions.”

The European Union also released a statement on Saturday, expressing “grave concern” over the humanitarian crisis.

It urged Israel to “allow immediate, unimpeded access” to humanitarian aid and “reopen all Gaza border crossings”.

Sunday’s joint appeal also called on all parties to “implement the Comprehensive Plan for Gaza”, a plan unveiled in 2025 that called for an immediate ceasefire between Israel and Hamas.

But attacks have continued, including on Thursday, when an Israeli air strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital killed six Palestinians.

Israel is the subject of an ongoing genocide case before the International Court of Justice, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former defence minister, Yoav Gallant, have been issued arrest warrants by the International Criminal Court.

They have been accused of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

articles.title: Cut national insurance for under-25s to create jobs, Milburn report to say
articles.summary: The report being launched this week will suggest gradually reducing employment costs over five years.
articles.body:
National Insurance (NI) paid by businesses on workers aged under 25 should be gradually lowered to encourage companies to create jobs for young people, a major review of youth unemployment will say.

A report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn will suggest the government should reduce NI costs over five years for people aged between 21 and 24 years old, starting in retail and hospitality.

Under Sir Keir Starmer, the government raised NI for firms. Milburn will say the number of young people not in employment, education or training - known as Neets - was not started by the NI rise.

But shadow work and pensions secretary, Helen Whately, said the government should "just stop doing the taxing".

The independent report, which has been in the works for a year and will be published on Tuesday, will also make recommendations on reducing the UK's benefits bill.

Milburn has said the government spends £22bn a year supporting young people who are economically inactive. There are nearly one million so-called Neets aged between 16 and 24 in the UK, according to data from the Office for National Statistics.

He will recommend that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide Universal Credit or personal independence payment (Pip), which is the main disability benefit in England and Wales.

Milburn wants the government to provide a legal guarantee of a job, training or employment support . Those who refuse to take up help could lose their benefits.

Milburn is also expected to say that helping young people develop skills is pointless if there are no jobs available for them.

The former health secretary will recommend doubling the threshold at which businesses start paying NI for 21 to 24-year-olds from £5,000 to £10,000.

But he will say this should only be done "when fiscal conditions allow".

Immediately axing NI for 21 to 24-year-olds would cost £5.1bn, according to research by the Resolution Foundation, a left-leaning think tank.

Milburn is set to say that given the UK's fiscal position, an immediate across-the-board cut in employer NI is not the best use of several billions of pounds of public money.

But Collette Osborne, a hairdresser who owns three salons in Nottingham, said she feels "suffocated by employment costs" including NI and the minimum wage.

She said she used to employ eight apprentices a year, now she cannot afford to take on any. Her workforce has more than halved to 21 staff.

Osborne told the BBC it costs "around £60,000 to train an apprentice before we can actually start allowing them onto customers' heads".

She said she has had parents so desperate for their children to find employment at her salons that some have even offered to pay their wages.

"I'm inundated with applications - and I mean inundated - which is heartbreaking because I can't take them on," she said.

Osborne does not feel she is getting help to offer jobs to youngsters.

"I feel like the government's foot is firmly on my neck," she said. "They promise breathing space. I feel suffocated, suffocated by employment costs."

Milburn told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme he agreed with a recent move by Chancellor John Healey to slow down the equalisation of the national minimum wage across age groups.

Labour had pledged in its manifesto to remove "discriminatory age bands" and close the gap between adult minimum wages and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.

But in his Budget, Healey said pay for that age group would rise from £10.85 to £11.27 an hour in April next year while people aged 21 and over will see their wages increase from £12.71 to £13.21.

"I understand why because nobody wants to see young workers on poverty pay," Milburn said, but he said it "imposed a lot of costs on [the] government".

"I think we have got to look very carefully at the convergence issue," he said.

Milburn said he supported the government subsidising wages to encourage businesses to take on young workers.

"Because young people today are walking into the workplace often with a mental health problem, ADHD or anxiety, if you're a small business that's a cost that you've got to absorb," he said.

"The state has a responsibility to help them with that."

On Sunday, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the government would extend its subsidised jobs guarantee scheme for 18 to 24-year-olds who are claiming Universal Credit.

People who have been on benefits for 12 months will be eligible, down from 18 months and the scheme would be available for people in England, Scotland and Wales.

McFadden said the scheme, which guarantees workers a six-month job, "will help more than 90,000 young people into work by March 2029".

But Whately said it is "just absurd that they are taxing businesses here and they're going to subsidise things that look like jobs over here. Just stop doing the taxing".

She said the Tories want to halve employer NI costs "because I talk to businesses who say they really want to employ young people but they just can't afford to anymore and the regulation that the Labour Party has put in place has made it harder".

Milburn will say that if the government does go ahead with a gradual reduction in NI over five years, it should start with businesses such as shops, bars and restaurants.

Retail and hospitality together provide 37% of jobs for young people aged between 16 and 24.

articles.title: Joe Biden calls Zelenskyy 'moody and stubborn,' questions his gratitude in new memoir
articles.summary: Joe Biden calls Volodymyr Zelenskyy "moody" and "not as grateful as I would have expected" in his forthcoming memoir, "Promise Me, America."
articles.body: Former President Joe Biden described Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as difficult in private and insufficiently grateful in a forthcoming memoir reviewed Friday by The Wall Street Journal, adding his assessment to a relationship President Donald Trump has also publicly criticized. Zelenskyy "could be moody and stubborn in our private conversations, and not as grateful as I would have expected," Biden said in "Promise Me, America," according to the newspaper. Zelenskyy previously addressed questions about his gratitude during a February 2025 interview with Fox News' Bret Baier on "Special Report," following his Oval Office clash with Trump and Vice President JD Vance. When Baier asked whether he owed Trump an apology, Zelenskyy emphasized his appreciation for American support. "I'm thankful to President Trump and to Congress, bipartisan support, and I was always very thankful from all our people," Zelenskyy said. TRUMP CALLS FOR UKRAINE TO REPLACE ZELENSKYY AFTER CLASH OVER RUSSIA DIESEL DEAL: 'GET A NEW PRESIDENT' In a November interview with Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst, Zelenskyy defended Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries despite objections from the Trump administration. Biden’s memoir also addresses his handling of the presidential transition and his concerns about the incoming Trump administration’s approach to negotiations with Moscow. According to the account, Trump’s team sought a letter authorizing direct negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin before Trump returned to office. Biden said he declined because of what he believed such talks could mean for Ukraine. KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION He was "unwilling to give them carte blanche for what I expected would be a kind of surrender, at Ukraine's expense," Biden said. The former president also offered a personal assessment of Putin’s behavior during their encounters, describing an effort to project disinterest. Putin "liked to slouch during a meeting, feigning indifference, like a teenager," Biden said. Biden’s criticism of Zelenskyy appears alongside a favorable assessment of the Ukrainian leader’s previous career. His acting background "turned out to be very good training," Biden said. ZELENSKYY CAN LEVERAGE MOSCOW TIES FROM COMEDY DAYS TO MAKE PEACE DEAL, SAYS FORMER KEY AIDE During Biden’s presidency, Ukraine’s requests included stronger air defenses, expanded weapons production and assistance disrupting Russian military logistics, according to a December 2023 account from Zelenskyy’s office. Before that White House meeting, Zelenskyy expressed appreciation for international assistance. "I’d like to thank America and our partners for their support," Zelenskyy said. His statement framed the measures as part of helping Ukraine defeat Russia’s invasion. "The United States will provide Ukraine with the support it needs to win this war," Biden said.
